Type Purpose Edit dialog vline / hline Vertical/horizontal reference line EditLineDialog text Free text label with optional background box EditTextDialog arrow Point-to-point arrow EditArrowDialog vspan / hspan Shaded vertical/horizontal band EditSpanDialog box Filled/outlined rectangle EditBoxDialog callout Text label with a pointer arrow to a data point EditCalloutDialog

All stored as typed dicts in MGraph.annotations. Every type supports drag interaction — clicking and dragging updates position in real time and emits annotation_position_changed — implemented by GraphAnnotationMixin._on_annotation_click()/_on_annotation_drag()/_on_annotation_release() in graphs/v_graph_annotations.py. Hit-testing is done manually (self.ax.findobj() + artist.contains(event)) rather than via matplotlib's pick_event: Figure.pick() only delivers a pick event to an artist when event.inaxes equals that artist's own Axes, which silently never happens for an annotation on the primary Axes whenever a secondary Y-axis is also present (it fully overlaps the primary Axes and has higher z-order, so event.inaxes resolves to it instead) — this used to make every annotation on a graph with y2/y3 configured completely undraggable. VGraph._ax_data_coords(event) resolves the drag position from the event's own pixel coordinates through self.ax.transData directly, sidestepping the same event.inaxes ambiguity for the position itself.

docs.title: Secondary & Inset Axes (TabSecondaryInset)
docs.text:
• Secondary Twin Axes: one row per Y2/Y3/X2 axis (each disabled until that axis has a column assigned), exposing Label, Min/Max, Log toggle, Color, and Marker — see Multi-Axis Support.
  • Inset (Zoom) Axes: a checkable group with Position (x0, y0) and Size (w, h) in axes-fraction coordinates, independent X/Y limits, and a "Show zoom indicator" toggle that draws the connector lines from the inset box back to the region it zooms into on the main plot (ax.indicate_inset_zoom()). The inset Axes itself is never persisted — it's rebuilt on every render from MGraph.inset_bounds. Mutually exclusive with a broken axis.

docs.title: Style Templates & Plot Recipes
docs.text:
Two conceptually distinct, previously-conflated features:

  • Plot Recipe (MPlotRecipeStore / VPlotRecipeDialog, folder: <working folder>/plot_recipe/) — a saved set of full plot configurations (data bindings and style: df_name, x/y/z, filters, plus every style field), one JSON file per recipe. Applying a recipe creates new plots: _on_recipe_applied() re-targets each saved config's df_name at the currently selected DataFrame (not each plot's originally-saved one) and skips + reports any plot whose required columns are missing, rather than aborting the whole batch. The whole recipe applies as one undo step. The dialog supports browse/search/apply/rename/duplicate/delete.
  • Style Template (MStyleTemplateStore / VStyleTemplateDialog, folder: <working folder>/plot_style/) — a saved appearance-only style dict (graph_style.extract_style()), one JSON file per template. Applying one (_apply_style_to_graph()) writes onto an existing graph via graph_style.apply_style_dict() — data bindings are never touched. A leaner sibling of VPlotRecipeDialog: no graph-count or Duplicate, since a style template is always exactly one style dict.

Both stores are deliberately rebuilt from the current Working Folder setting at the point of use (VWorkspaceGraphs._refresh_recipe_and_style_stores(), called at the top of every apply/save handler, including the AI Chat panel's own recipe-save flow via VMChat.refresh_recipe_store()) rather than built once at startup — fixing a bug where a Working Folder configured after the workspace tab already existed silently never took effect until an app restart.

Each VGraph's toolbar Style menu ties these together: Save Style… / Apply Style… (open the respective dialog), Copy Style / Paste Style (in-memory, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V), Reset to Default (always the hardcoded factory graph_style.default_style()), and Set as Default Style (saves the current graph's style, via MSettings.set_default_graph_style(), as the baseline new graphs start from — see Data Flow: Creating a Plot). These are two independent, non-overlapping concepts: Reset to Default always restores the factory style regardless of what's been set as default; Set as Default Style only changes what newly created plots start with, is persisted across restarts, and never affects existing graphs or Reset-to-Default's behavior.

docs.title: Export & Multi-Panel Composer
docs.text:
File: spectroview/view/components/graphs/v_export_dialog.py

  • VExportDialog(graph_widget, parent=None) — exports a single graph to PNG/TIFF/SVG/PDF/EPS with format/DPI/transparency/export-time-theme-override controls, plus a physical-size section (journal presets, mm/inch toggle, blank = current on-screen size) that persists back onto the graph's export_width_mm/export_height_mm fields.
  • VBatchExportDialog(graph_widgets: dict, parent=None) — exports every currently-open graph to a chosen folder in one pass, each at its own already-persisted physical size, reporting per-graph failures in a summary dialog.

File: spectroview/view/components/graphs/v_multipanel_dialog.py

  • VMultiPanelDialog(graph_widgets: dict, parent=None) — composes several checked/reordered open graphs into one throwaway matplotlib.figure.Figure grid (auto-suggested rows/cols, constrained layout, shared-axis-label collapsing on interior panels, lettered/numbered panel labels). Each panel is rendered by temporarily repointing the source VGraph's .ax/.figure onto the composed figure's subplot and calling its normal render path, then restoring the source widget so the live workspace is never mutated. Graphs with an active broken axis render via a simplified single-panel path in the composed figure (a documented scope limit).

AI/MCP exposes the persistent per-graph export size (export_width_mm / export_height_mm) and on-screen geometry/DPI through GraphPatch. The actual Export/Batch Export and Multi-Panel actions remain GUI workflows: format, destination path, transparency, export-time theme, graph selection/order, and panel grid are one-off file/composition choices rather than MGraph state.

docs.title: MDI Area Management
docs.text:
The Graphs workspace uses a QMdiArea to display multiple plots simultaneously:

graph LR
    MDI["QMdiArea"] --> SW1["SubWindow 1"]
    MDI --> SW2["SubWindow 2"]
    MDI --> SW3["SubWindow 3"]
    SW1 --> VG1["VGraph"]
    SW2 --> VG2["VGraph"]
    SW3 --> VG3["VGraph"]
  • Each plot is wrapped in a QMdiSubWindow for independent sizing, minimizing, and arranging. Fusion's native subwindow frame is fairly thick and heavily beveled; self.mdi_area.setStyleSheet(...) adds a QMdiSubWindow { border: 1px solid ... } rule to flatten it to a thin 1px line (setting any border property via QSS switches a widget from native to CSS-based border rendering).
  • The bottom toolbar provides global controls: minimize/delete-all, Undo/Redo, Compose Figure (icon-only buttons, moved here from the side panel since they're workspace-global and used more often than the recipe buttons that stayed there), and one shared graph toolbar slot (self.graph_toolbar_slot / self._graph_toolbar_slot_layout, given stretch factor 1 so it fills the remaining width). Every VGraph builds its own matplotlib nav toolbar (Home/Pan/Zoom/Subplots) + a QFrame.VLine separator + action-button row (Replicate/Customize/Copy/Export/Style menu, pushed flush against the right edge via a QHBoxLayout.addStretch() between the separator and the buttons) in create_plot_widget(), but keeps it parentless and hidden (self.toolbar_container) instead of showing it inside its own MDI window — each MDI window shows only its plot canvas. The Export button does double duty (VGraph._on_export_clicked(), mirroring VSpectraViewer's Copy button): a plain click emits export_requested(graph_id) (single-graph export dialog); Ctrl+Click (checked via QApplication.keyboardModifiers() & Qt.ControlModifier inside the click handler) emits export_all_requested instead, wired to the same VWorkspaceGraphs._on_export_all_clicked() the old side-panel "Export All" button used to call — that button was removed outright once this made it redundant. Every action-button icon is a fixed colorful icon set once at creation; VGraph.update_icon_colors() and VWorkspaceGraphs's per-theme retinting of it were removed since nothing on a graph needs to track the app theme anymore. VWorkspaceGraphs._sync_active_graph_toolbar() reparents whichever graph's toolbar_container belongs to the currently active MDI subwindow into the shared slot (detaching the previous one first), so every graph visually shares one toolbar instead of each carrying an identical copy. It's called from every place the active graph can change or a graph's toolbar gets rebuilt: _on_subwindow_activated (covers subwindow clicks, the graph-list combobox, and the "no subwindows left" None case), _build_graph_widget (new graph), _on_update_plot/the AI-agent's graph-update path in main.py (create_plot_widget() rebuilds toolbar_container from scratch, so the slot must re-sync to the new instance), and _on_graph_closed/_on_delete_all/clear_workspace/_rebuild_all_graph_widgets (teardown/rebuild paths, so the slot never dangles a reference to a deleted widget). X-label rotation and the grid toggle used to live in this toolbar too — moved into the Customize dialog's General & Typography tab (TabGeneral, alongside Figure theme) since they're per-graph style, not workspace-global, and the toolbar versions only ever applied as one-off new-plot defaults with no live-preview. (A DPI spinbox used to live here too — removed: it only ever set the default DPI for the next newly-created plot, silently doing nothing when changed with an existing graph selected despite visually syncing to show that graph's DPI, which read as a live edit control but wasn't one. MGraph.dpi still defaults to 100 and can be set via script/AI-agent; on-screen rendering resolution isn't something users need to hand-tune day to day, and export resolution has its own explicit control in VExportDialog.)
  • The graph selector combobox ("Active plot:") and the live plot-size label both moved out of the bottom toolbar: the selector now lives in the side panel, right above Add/Update Plot (VWorkspaceGraphs._setup_action_buttons()), and the plot-size label was removed entirely (along with MdiSubWindow's figsize_label param and its now-pointless resizeEvent override).
  • "Minimize All" collapses all windows for a clean workspace.
  • Graph selection in the combobox activates the corresponding subwindow and syncs the right panel controls.

docs.title: Graph Storage
docs.text:
# VWorkspaceGraphs maintains a lookup:
self.graph_widgets = {
    graph_id: (VGraph, QDialog, QMdiSubWindow)
}

When a graph is selected via the combobox or by clicking its subwindow:

  1. _on_subwindow_activated() identifies the graph_id.
  2. The ViewModel's MGraph is loaded.
  3. The right panel controls (X/Y/Z comboboxes, labels, style) are synced to match.

docs.title: SPECTROview Working Folder
docs.text:
A single universal user-configured root folder (Settings panel) with five subfolders and a portable configuration file auto-created under it (os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)) on first configuration:

Subfolder / File Purpose MSettings getter fit_model/ Fit-model JSON templates (Spectra/Maps workspaces) get_fit_model_folder() plot_recipe/ Plot Recipes get_plot_recipe_folder() plot_style/ Style Templates get_plot_style_folder() ai_chat_history/ AI chat conversation history get_history_folder() / get_ai_history_folder() template/ User templates and custom presets get_template_folder() config.json Portable configuration backup export_config() / import_config()

get_working_folder() one-time-migrates from the older, separate "Fit model folder"/"Plot template folder" settings if either was previously configured, so existing setups aren't orphaned. A separate setting, get_default_graph_style()/set_default_graph_style(), stores the "Set as Default Style" baseline (see Style Templates & Plot Recipes) — unrelated to the working folder, but persisted the same way (QSettings, disk-backed, survives restarts).

docs.title: Save Format (.graphs)
docs.text:
Current format (format_version: 4) is a ZIP archive, written by WorkspaceIO.save_workspace(). Version 4 preserves x_as_numeric=False as the explicit Category selection; older versions keep their legacy False-to-Auto migration:

metadata.json                          # {"format_version": 4, "plots": {...}, "dataframe_sources": {...}}
dataframes/<name>.parquet              # one Parquet file per DataFrame, streamed directly into the zip

Each entry in metadata["plots"] is a full MGraph.save() dict keyed by graph_id:

{
    "plots": {
        "1": {
            "graph_id": 1,
            "df_name": "fit_results",
            "plot_style": "point",
            "x": "Slot",
            "y": ["Si_center"],
            "z": "Zone",
            "filters": [{"expression": "R² > 0.95", "state": true}],
            "legend_properties": [...],
            "annotations": [...],
            "plot_width": 480,
            "plot_height": 400,
            "dpi": 100
        }
    },
    "dataframe_sources": {
        "fit_results": "/path/to/original.xlsx"
    }
}

WorkspaceIO.load_workspace() sniffs the ZIP magic number; files that predate this format (raw JSON, DataFrames embedded as gzip-compressed CSV hex strings under an original_dfs key) are detected as legacy and loaded via a dedicated fallback path — kept only for opening old files, never used for saving.

docs.title: Plot Replication
docs.text:
The "Replicate" button (in the shared graph toolbar, acting on whichever graph is active) creates a deep copy of the plot:

  1. Serializes the current MGraph via save().
  2. Removes graph_id (the ViewModel assigns a new one).
  3. Captures the current subwindow size for the replica.
  4. Calls _create_and_display_plot() with the cloned config.

This enables rapid A/B comparison of the same data with different visual settings. Unlike newly-created plots (Add Plot / Add Multi-Wafer), a replicated graph's style is not overridden by the "Set as Default Style" baseline, since it already carries a fully-specified, intentional style.

docs.title: Workspace: Maps
docs.text:
The Maps workspace handles hyperspectral map data — spatially resolved spectral datasets where each pixel corresponds to a full spectrum. It extends the Spectra workspace via inheritance, gaining all fitting, baseline, peak-editing, and persistence capabilities for free, and adds spatial awareness, heatmap visualization, and coordinate-based operations on top.

[!NOTE] Prerequisites — Before reading this guide, ensure you are familiar with:

  • Data Architecture: SpectraStore — the shared MapData / SpectraStore data model.
  • Workspace: Spectra — the base ViewModel, View components, and data flow patterns.

This page covers only the Maps-specific extensions. Inherited behavior is not repeated here.

docs.title: How Maps Differs from Spectra
docs.text:
The fundamental difference is the cardinality of MapData.N:

Workspace MapData.N Meaning Spectra 1 One spectrum per MapData block Maps 2 – 100 000 N spectra sharing a single wavenumber axis

Because the underlying tensor model is identical, a single vectorized fit that works for 1 spectrum also works for 100 000, with no code change in the engine.

docs.title: MapData in Maps Context
docs.text:
MapData ("wafer_300mm") — 50×50 wafer (2500 spectra, 1000 wavenumbers)
├── x0:          float64[1000]          1 shared wavenumber axis
├── Y0:          float32[2500, 1000]    raw intensities — 10 MB
├── x:           float64[800]           after spectral crop
├── Y:           float32[2500, 800]     after crop + baseline sub — 8 MB
├── coords:      float64[2500, 2]       (X, Y) stage positions in µm
├── fnames:      list[str] × 2500       "wafer_300mm_(x_pos, y_pos)"
├── is_active:   bool[2500]             checkbox state
├── peak_params: float64[2500, K]       after VBF fit — all 2500 at once
├── fit_success: bool[2500]
├── fit_r2:      float64[2500]
├── Y_bestfit:   float32[2500, 800]     8 MB
└── Y_peaks:     [float32[2500, 800], ...]   8 MB per peak

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph View ["View Layer"]
        VWM["VWorkspaceMaps<br/>(extends VWorkspaceSpectra)"]
        ML["VMapsList<br/>(maps list + actions)"]
        MV["VMapViewer<br/>(Matplotlib heatmap)"]
        MVD["VMapViewerDialog<br/>(detachable viewer)"]
        SV_inh["VSpectraViewer<br/>(inherited)"]
        FMB_inh["VFitModelBuilder<br/>(inherited)"]
    end

    subgraph VM ["ViewModel Layer"]
        VMWM["VMWorkspaceMaps<br/>(extends VMWorkspaceSpectra)"]
        VMWS_inh["VMWorkspaceSpectra<br/>(base class)"]
    end

    subgraph Model ["Model Layer"]
        SS["SpectraStore"]
        IO["m_io<br/>(map file loaders)"]
        VBF["VBFthread<br/>(mega-batch fit)"]
        WIO["WorkspaceIO"]
    end

    VWM --> ML & MV & MVD
    VWM --> SV_inh & FMB_inh
    VWM -->|"method calls"| VMWM
    VMWM -.->|"extends"| VMWS_inh
    VMWM -->|"Qt signals"| VWM
    VMWM --> SS & IO & VBF & WIO

docs.title: Why Inheritance Instead of Composition?
docs.text:
VMWorkspaceMaps extends VMWorkspaceSpectra rather than wrapping it:

  • Every fitting algorithm (baseline, peaks, VBF engine) works identically on both single spectra (N=1) and maps (N>1).
  • Duplicating or delegating the fitting code would introduce maintenance fragility.
  • Overriding via the Template Method pattern (three hook methods) is sufficient to customize bulk-operation targeting without forking any algorithm logic.

The same pattern applies at the View level: VWorkspaceMaps extends VWorkspaceSpectra, overrides setup_connections() to prevent double-wiring during __init__, then replaces the right sidebar widget with the map-specific VMapsList + VMapViewer panel.

docs.title: VMWorkspaceMaps — The ViewModel
docs.text:
File: vm_workspace_maps.py (with fitting/persistence mixins in spectroview/viewmodel/maps/)

Additional state beyond the inherited VMWorkspaceSpectra:

Attribute Type Purpose maps dict[str, pd.DataFrame] Raw map DataFrames indexed by name (legacy cache) current_map_name str \| None Active map selection maps_metadata dict[str, dict] Acquisition metadata per map (WDF, SPC, L6M, NGC) map_type str '2Dmap' or 'Wafer_300mm' / 'Wafer_200mm' / 'Wafer_100mm' graphs_workspace ref Injected reference for profile extraction

docs.title: Additional Signals
docs.text:
maps_list_changed       = Signal(list)    # map name list updated → VMapsList
map_data_updated        = Signal(object)  # current map DF changed → trigger heatmap redraw
send_spectra_to_workspace = Signal(list)  # deep copies → Spectra workspace
clear_map_cache_requested = Signal(str)   # map name → VMapViewer cache invalidation
switch_to_graphs_tab    = Signal()        # request tab switch after profile extraction

docs.title: Additional Method Reference
docs.text: Category Methods Map loading load_map_files(paths) Map selection & order select_map(name), select_maps(names, primary), reorder_maps(new_order), _show_map_spectra(name) Map deletion delete_current_map(), remove_map(name) Map data get_current_map_dataframe(), get_fit_results_dataframe() Export save_current_map_to_csv(file_path) Fit fit(), _run_fit_thread(), collect_fit_results() — all override parent Cross-workspace send_selected_spectra_to_spectra_workspace(), extract_and_send_profile_to_graphs() Persistence save_work(), load_work(), _load_legacy_maps()

docs.title: VWorkspaceMaps — The View
docs.text:
File: v_workspace_maps.py

Overrides _add_maps_panel() to replace the inherited spectra sidebar with:

  • VMapViewer — the heatmap canvas with Z-parameter and X-range sliders.
  • VMapsList — maps list panel with map management and spectra action buttons.

The left side (SpectraViewer + bottom tabs) is inherited from VWorkspaceSpectra. While VWorkspaceSpectra initializes VLiveMaps and VMLiveMaps in "spectra" mode (rendering 1D parameter variation graphs across the currently selected spectra), VWorkspaceMaps switches the inherited v_live_maps and vm_live_maps instances to "map" mode (set_mode("map")).

In the Maps workspace, when maps are loaded or selected, VWorkspaceMaps synchronizes a Two-Tier selection model:

  • Primary Map (VMWorkspaceMaps.current_map_name): Drives preprocessing, fitting, VMapViewer, VSpectraViewer, MVA, and More metadata identically to single-selection workflows.
  • Selected Map List (VMWorkspaceMaps.selected_map_names): Populated via VMapsList (QAbstractItemView.ExtendedSelection), enabling Ctrl+Click / Shift+Click comparison without altering Primary operations or triggering VMapViewer redraws when the Primary stays unchanged.

VWorkspaceMaps forwards [MapData, ...] plus primary_name to self.vm_live_maps.set_map_datas(...) only when the Live Maps tab is active (otherwise flagging _live_maps_dirty = True for a single lazy flush upon tab activation, while VMapViewer spatial point clicks are ignored). Activating an R/B/G bracket on VSpectraViewer automatically switches bottom_tabs to Live Maps in VWorkspaceSpectra._on_range_selector_toggled() and flushes any pending selection immediately. VMLiveMaps inspects md.coords via cached analyze_map_geometry() and build_map_gridder() (which caches regular grid indices or Delaunay barycentric vertex/weights until coords or is_active change), excludes unchecked spectra (~md.is_active), caches per-parameter slices across drags using (id(md), md.name, md.data_version, param, range), and applies Primary-Precedence dimensionality adaptation:

  • Primary is 1D profile: Emits multi_profile_data_ready (when \(\ge 2\) profiles) or profile_data_ready (single profile), overlaying all selected 1D profiles in matched colors (DEFAULT_COLORS) with uniform line thickness and any excluded 2D maps noted in the context header.
  • Primary is 2D map: Populates map_2d_candidates_changed for the tab's [◀ | ComboBox | ▶] 2D map switcher, excludes 1D profiles, and computes/renders only the single currently visible 2D heatmap via map_data_ready.
  • Red/Blue Intensity Ratio (R/B ratio): Computes \(I_{\mathrm{Red}} / I_{\mathrm{Blue}}\) dynamically across both single/multi-1D profiles and 2D heatmaps, masking zero/near-zero Blue intensities and unchecked spectra as NaN. While R/B ratio is selected in the Green channel, VWorkspaceSpectra._on_range_selector_parameter_changed() notifies VSpectraViewer.set_range_selector_parameter() so the Green range bracket is hidden on the spectrum canvas (and restored as soon as another spectral parameter is selected).

For massive batches (>= 25,000 active spectra by default via ASYNC_SPECTRUM_THRESHOLD), VMLiveMaps offloads pure-NumPy evaluation and gridding to a single-worker QThreadPool (_LiveMapWorker) bridged via a parented QObject (_LiveMapWorkerBridge) with monotonic _generation_id cancellation and clean shutdown() teardown on exit. VMLiveMaps also emits spatial_sites_changed (carrying ordered active site coordinates, optional 1D profile positions, and target map name) so Live Maps panels stay aligned with the active dataset. On the UI side, the RGB bracketing and Live Maps widgets live together under spectroview/view/components/rgb_live_maps/ (v_live_maps.py, v_live_maps_options.py, v_live_map_subpanel.py, v_live_map_1d.py, v_live_map_2d.py, v_live_map_selection.py, v_live_maps_legend_editor.py, v_range_selector.py, v_range_bracket_mixin.py, common.py). VLiveMaps provides persistent Show Legend and a compact 2-column More view options (btn_legend / btn_options) menu matching VSpectraViewer row spacing ((2, 2, 2, 2) margins) for instant client-side restyling at a crisp 96 DPI baseline: independent Plot theme ("Light Mode" default vs "Dark Mode", decoupled from global Qt UI icons via apply_global_theme()), Linear/Log X, Y, and Z color scaling with non-positive domain guards, line/dot/line+dots plot styles (default "line"), line width (1.5), dot size (1.5), graph text size (6–24 pt), Copied figure size (copy_fig_width/copy_fig_height, default 5.5 × 4.0 in) & Copied figure theme (Light Mode/Dark Mode) so clipboard figures are rendered at fixed physical size/aspect independent of window resizing, legend placement/columns/font size, LiveMapsLegendEditorDialog for custom canvas legend labels & colors, shared 1D Y-axis synchronization (restoring per-panel bounds when toggled off), axes figure label toggle (show_figure_label, default Off), warning-free gridlines (default Off), heatmap smoothing, and colorbar visibility. View options persist across restarts in MSettings (live_maps_view_options/*, debounced 250 ms save and exit flush) and cross-sync between Spectra and Maps workspaces. Each LiveMapSubpanel also embeds per-panel Rescale, Pan, and Zoom buttons synchronized bidirectionally with NoDoubleClickZoomToolbar (preserving legend double-click editing), supports dual-mode Copy (btn_copy: plain click copies the figure canvas at fixed copy_fig_width × copy_fig_height and copy_fig_theme; Ctrl + Click emits copy_data_requested(color_id) and copies the underlying tabular data as TSV via copy_df_to_clb() across 1D series, single/multi-1D profiles, and 2D (X, Y, Value) points backed by VMLiveMaps.get_2d_copy_points() with _grid/_extent fallback), swaps the 2D colormap picker on Row 2 for per-panel view-only 1D Normalization controls (btn_norm, norm_xmin, norm_xmax, backed by _normalize_1d_values() and normalized _get_primary_profile_values() / reset_view() + normalization_changed \(\rightarrow\) _sync_shared_y()) whenever 1D line plots are displayed, shares spatial geometry (compute_2d_spatial_geometry()), click/Ctrl+Click/marquee selection resolution (resolve_xy_selection() / resolve_1d_profile_selection()), and red selection overlays (MapCanvasSelector) with VMapViewer via map_selection.py whenever Pan/Zoom tools and legend boxes are inactive (routing VLiveMaps.spectra_selected through VWorkspaceMaps._on_live_maps_point_selection() to update VSpectraViewer, VMapViewer, dialog viewers, and all R/B/G panels without recalculating grids), while fast UI restyling (apply_view_options_fast()), @lru_cache mplstyle dicts (_get_cached_style_dict), settled-layout freezing (_on_canvas_draw / _request_relayout), and parented 35 ms coalesced redraw timers keep interactive option changes stall-free.

Range selector updates adaptively debounce (60–250 ms) during continuous motion and flush immediately on mouse release (VSpectraViewer.range_drag_finished \(\rightarrow\) VMLiveMaps.flush_pending()). During bracket dragging, RangeSelectorManager.render() updates existing Matplotlib artists in-place (set_animated(True) with Agg background blitting and temporary layout_engine suspension via SpectraRangeBracketMixin on VSpectraViewer plus horizontal clamping via transData.inverted()), while LiveMapSubpanel fast-path updates (update_series() / update_multi_profile()) cache theme/text-size/grid/X-domain signatures (_invalidate_style_caches()) and MapCanvasSelector.draw_1d_overlay() reuses existing 1D selection markers in-place to eliminate tick_params()/AutoLocator() redraw churn. Range selector artists use Matplotlib's ax.add_artist() so that ax.dataLim is never polluted, ensuring that the Rescale button (Ctrl+R) zooms exclusively to spectral data.

Centralized map type management: The selected_map_type attribute is the single source of truth for all viewers (main + dialogs). When the user changes the combobox in any viewer, _on_map_type_changed() updates all viewers synchronously, preventing drift.

docs.title: VMapViewer — The Heatmap Canvas
docs.text:
Package: map_viewer/ (v_map_viewer.py, v_map_plot.py, v_map_data.py, v_map_interactions.py, map_selection.py)

The most complex View component (~1 300 lines). It renders both 2D rectangular maps and circular wafer maps. Features:

  • Z-parameter combobox (Intensity / Area / any fit result column)
  • X-range double slider (filters which wavenumbers contribute to Z)
  • Outlier removal toggle
  • Accurate Spatial Coordinate Placement: For regular Cartesian grids, renders via fast imshow with symmetric extent bounds. For irregular or scattered coordinates (such as wafer map files loaded in 2Dmap mode), automatically renders square pixel patches centered at each point's exact \((X, Y)\) coordinate via PatchCollection, completely eliminating spatial drift between heatmap pixels and selection overlays.
  • Color-scale combobox (Linear / Log) in the options (…) menu — _build_color_kwargs() returns a matplotlib.colors.LogNorm for "Log" (falling back to plain linear vmin/vmax when the Z-range isn't strictly positive, since intensity/area are clipped >=0 and fit parameters can be <=0); applies to both the 2Dmap imshow and the wafer griddata imshow
  • Interactive selection (click, rectangle drag, profile line)
  • In-Place Artist Updates & Dataset Isolation: For parameter, X-range, or palette changes on the currently active map (_last_rendered_map_name == map_df_name), _do_plot_heatmap_internal() fast-paths by updating self.img (set_data / set_array, set_extent, set_clim) and self.cbar.update_normal(...) in-place, bypassing destructive figure.clf(), subplot re-creation, and expensive tight_layout(). When switching between different map datasets or map types, a clean axes rebuild executes while reusing cached (heatmap_pivot, extent, vmin, vmax, grid_z, final_z_col, dx, dy) from _griddata_cache.
  • Fast Z-Range Slider Updates: Real-time slider drag events bypass cache key recomputations and map repaints, updating set_clim() / set_norm() and colorbar directly in-place.
  • Vector Navigation Controls & Built-in Coordinates: Interactive navigation buttons (btn_home / btn_rescale, btn_pan, btn_zoom) styled identically to SPECTROview toolbar controls (28x28, @surface_elevated, rounded corners) and vector SVG icons (Icons.rescale(), Icons.pan(), Icons.zoom()), replacing default matplotlib icons while maintaining bidirectional mode synchronization with NavigationToolbar2QT. The native matplotlib toolbar is completely hidden in the background, and live coordinates are rendered cleanly using a dedicated native lbl_coordinates label (min-width: 180px, @text_secondary, right-aligned) without clipping or layout shifting.
  • Multi-viewer dialog spawning

docs.title: VMapsList — The Maps List & Actions Panel
docs.text:
File: v_map_list.py

Displays loaded map names in an internal _ReorderableMapsList(QListWidget) (ExtendedSelection for Shift+Click / Ctrl+Click multi-selection with Primary focus tracking via maps_selection_changed(selected_names, primary_name), plus InternalMove drag-and-drop reordering emitting maps_order_changed(new_order) while ignoring external URL MIME drops so file drops propagate to parent windows). On internal drop, selection and Primary focus are preserved without transient selection churn and forwarded to VMWorkspaceMaps.reorder_maps(), which reorders self.maps, SpectraStore.reorder_maps(), and selected_map_names and refreshes both VMapsList and Live Maps without resetting VMapViewer. Paired with quick management buttons (View, Delete — prompting confirmation when deleting multiple selected maps, Export CSV) and unified spectra action buttons (Select All, Reinitialize, Fitting Statistics, Send to Spectra Workspace) targeting the Primary map and its spatially selected spectra.

docs.title: VMapViewerDialog — Detachable Window
docs.text:
File: v_map_viewer_dialog.py

A QDialog wrapper around a second VMapViewer instance. Uses Qt.WindowStaysOnTopHint so the user can select pixels in the floating window while the main window shows the spectrum. Multiple dialogs can be open simultaneously, each showing a different Z-parameter on the same spatial data. Data is shared by reference — no duplication.

docs.title: The Dual-Storage Pattern
docs.text:
The Maps workspace maintains two stores for the same data:

  1. self.maps[map_name] — a pd.DataFrame with columns X, Y, w1, w2, ... (one row per spectrum). This is the legacy store populated at load time from the file parser.
  2. self.store.get_map_data(map_name) — the MapData tensor block with all processing state.

The DataFrame is used for heatmap input (pivot table → imshow) and CSV export. The tensor block is used for all analysis operations (baseline, fitting, results collection). When saving processed data to CSV, save_current_map_to_csv() reads from md.x / md.Y (processed) rather than the raw DataFrame.

[!IMPORTANT] When a new developer is confused about "where is the data?", the answer is: both places, for different purposes. The DataFrame is the entry point from the file loader and the input to the heatmap pipeline. The tensor block is the source of truth for all analysis. Modifications (baseline, crop) only affect the tensor block — they do not update the DataFrame.

docs.title: Filename Convention
docs.text:
Each spectrum row in a MapData block gets a unique fname constructed from its coordinates:

fname = f"{map_name}_({float(x_pos)}, {float(y_pos)})"
# Example: "wafer_300mm_(12.5, -7.0)"

This convention is used throughout the codebase to:

  • Filter spectra belonging to a specific map: fname.startswith(f"{map_name}_(")
  • Extract coordinates from fnames: parse between ( and ).
  • Match SpectraStore entries back to DataFrame rows for heatmap rendering.

Coordinate parsing is centralized in parse_coords_from_fname() (viewmodel/common/spectral_utils.py, re-exported in viewmodel/utils.py); VWorkspaceMaps._extract_coords_from_fname() and VMWorkspaceMaps._extract_coords_for_spectra() both delegate to it. If you change the fname convention, update that single helper (and keep the float() formatting identical on the write side in _extract_spectra_from_map()).

docs.title: Loading a Hyperspectral Map
docs.text:
1. User Action: The user initiates a load map action in VWorkspaceMaps.
  2. View → ViewModel: The View calls vm.load_map_files(paths).
  3. File Parsing: For each file, the ViewModel delegates to the m_io module (load_wdf_map, load_spc_map, load_l6m_map, load_ngc_map, etc.). The IO module returns a DataFrame containing X, Y, and all wavenumber columns, plus metadata.
  4. Data Storage (Legacy): The ViewModel caches the returned DataFrame in self.maps[name].
  5. Data Extraction: The ViewModel calls _extract_spectra_from_map(name, map_df), which delegates to extract_map_arrays(name, map_df) in m_io.py to extract the x0, Y0, and spatial coords arrays from the DataFrame and build the pixel fnames list.
  6. Data Storage (Tensor): The ViewModel registers the data in the SpectraStore via add_map(name, x0, Y0, coords, fnames, is_active).
  7. UI Update: Once all files are processed, the ViewModel emits the maps_list_changed signal with the list of loaded map names.

extract_map_arrays() filters out any trailing or non-numeric Unnamed: columns while preserving all valid numeric wavenumber channels, and automatically appends _{k} suffixes to fnames only when duplicate (X, Y) spatial coordinates occur (e.g., time-resolved multi-scan maps at fixed wafer sites).

docs.title: Map Selection
docs.text:
When the user clicks a map name in VMapsList or opens a new map:

  1. User Action: The user opens a map file or clicks a map name in the VMapsList UI widget.
  2. View → ViewModel: The View captures this and calls vm.select_map(map_name).
  3. State Update & Auto-Selection: The ViewModel sets current_map_name = map_name, populates _show_map_spectra(map_name), and automatically selects the first spectrum self.selected_fnames = [md.fnames[0]], emitting spectra_selection_changed to immediately plot the first spectrum in VSpectraViewer.
  4. Map Viewer Refresh: The ViewModel emits map_data_updated(current_map_df).
  5. Canvas Redraw & Selection Overlay: VWorkspaceMaps forwards the updated data to VMapViewer.set_map_data(), which automatically highlights the first coordinate (x_0, y_0) with the red selection overlay and calls plot_heatmap() to render the spatial data. Floating viewer dialogs are kept in sync.

docs.title: Fitting Workflow (Maps Override)
docs.text:
The Maps workspace overrides fit() to construct multi-task batches that can span the entire map:

  1. User Action: The user clicks "Fit" (or Ctrl+Fit to apply to all maps).
  2. Task Construction:
    • If apply_all = True: The ViewModel groups maps by x-axis length and stacks them into mega-batch Y matrices.
    • If apply_all = False: The ViewModel builds a task for just the current map and selected indices.
  3. Thread Launch: The ViewModel starts a VBFthread with the task list.
  4. Engine Execution (Background): For each task, the thread calls VBFengine.fit_spectra(). Stacked multi-map tasks are fit as a single vectorized operation.
  5. Result Storage (Background): The thread scatters results back to their respective maps via SpectraStore.set_fit_results().
  6. Completion: The thread emits finished(), and the ViewModel calls _on_fit_finished().
  7. Result Collection: collect_fit_results() aggregates the results into a single DataFrame.
  8. UI Refresh: Signals are emitted to redraw both the heatmap (map_data_updated) and the results table (fit_results_updated).

Mega-batch grouping is the key performance optimization. When apply_all=True, maps with the same x-axis length are stacked into a single Y matrix and fit in one vectorized call. A 10-map wafer measurement that individually takes 30 s each can complete in ~35 s total when batched.

docs.title: After Fitting: Propagating Results
docs.text:
After _on_fit_finished():

  1. collect_fit_results() is called → builds self.df_fit_results (DataFrame with X, Y columns + all fit columns).
  2. fit_results_updated emitted → VFitResults table updates.
  3. map_data_updated emitted → VMapViewer re-reads df_fit_results and adds fit columns to its Z-parameter combobox.
  4. clear_map_cache_requested emitted → VMapViewer invalidates its griddata cache for the affected map name.

docs.title: Map Visualization Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Data Source: Depending on preprocessing state, the source is either the processed intensities (md.Y) or raw intensities (md.Y0).
  2. DataFrame Filtering: get_current_map_dataframe() filters out inactive spectra.
  3. Viewer Binding: The DataFrame is passed to VMapViewer.set_map_data().
  4. Z-Value Computation: _compute_z_values() calculates the target metric based on the combobox selection:
    • Intensity: sums over the selected X-range slider.
    • Area: calculates a trapezoidal integral.
    • Fit parameter: retrieves values directly from df_fit_results.
  5. Outlier Removal: Z-values are clipped using percentiles if the user toggles the feature.
  6. Rendering Logic: Depending on map_type:
    • 2D map: Fast path. A pivot table maps (X, Y) to Z on an exact grid, rendered via Matplotlib imshow().
    • Wafer map: Slow path. scipy.griddata interpolates irregular circular sites onto an 80×80 grid before rendering via imshow().

Why two rendering paths?

A 2D rectangular map has data on a regular grid — a pivot table suffices and renders in milliseconds. A wafer measurement has sites distributed across a circular region (not a grid), so scipy.griddata must interpolate onto a regular grid before imshow can render it. This is the expensive step.

docs.title: Heatmap Caching Strategy
docs.text:
scipy.griddata can take 100–500 ms for large maps. The viewer uses a multi-key cache to avoid recomputation:

cache_key = (
    map_name,        # which map
    parameter,       # which Z parameter
    (xmin, xmax),    # X-range filter
    map_type,        # 2Dmap vs Wafer variant
    mask_config,     # mask settings or None
    remove_outliers  # outlier removal flag
)

The cache stores (heatmap_pivot, extent, vmin, vmax, grid_z, final_z_col, dx, dy), retaining exact pixel spatial dimensions (dx, dy) across map type switches and file selections to prevent cross-dataset geometry drift.

The cache is:

  • Preserved across map switches — switching back to a previously viewed map is instant, restoring its exact spatial dimensions and griddata.
  • Invalidated by name after fitting completes, via the clear_map_cache_requested signal.
  • Not persisted across application sessions — it lives only in VMapViewer._griddata_cache.
  • Dataset-isolated: can_fast_update requires _last_rendered_map_name == map_df_name and checks PatchCollection patch count, ensuring in-place artist updates only execute on the active dataset while dataset switches always trigger a clean redraw.

docs.title: Interactive Selection
docs.text:
The VMapViewer supports three selection modes:

Mode Trigger Behavior Single click Left-click on map Selects nearest site, highlights with red rectangle Rectangle drag Click-and-drag Selects all sites within dragged rectangle Profile Exactly 2 selected sites, 2D mode Enables "Extract profile" button

Selection in VMapViewer emits spectra_selected(list[tuple]). VWorkspaceMaps._on_map_viewer_selection() maps the (x, y) coordinates back to fnames and calls vm.set_selected_fnames(), which triggers _emit_selected_spectra() → VSpectraViewer redraws the selected spectrum.

Selected points are rendered as PatchCollection (one draw call for all rectangles) rather than individual add_patch() calls, giving O(1) rendering time regardless of selection size.

docs.title: Template Method Overrides
docs.text: The Maps workspace customizes the inherited bulk-operation pipeline via three hook methods. Understanding these is essential when debugging or extending bulk operations.

docs.title: _get_target_mds(apply_all)
docs.text:
Determines which MapData objects a bulk operation targets.

apply_all Spectra workspace Maps workspace False MapData blocks of selected spectra Current map's MapData block only True All MapData blocks in store All maps' MapData blocks

This is why Ctrl+Subtract-Baseline in the Maps workspace subtracts from all spectra in the current map (not just selected ones) — the Maps override returns the entire map's MapData.

docs.title: _on_map_data_changed(md, action)
docs.text:
Called after each individual MapData is modified within a bulk loop.

# Maps workspace override:
def _on_map_data_changed(self, md, action: str):
    if action == "reinit_spectra":
        self.store.clear_preprocess(md.name)
    elif action in ("delete_baseline", "subtract_baseline", "apply_spectral_range"):
        self.store.batch_preprocess(md.name, md.baseline_config, md.range_min, md.range_max)
    elif action == "paste_peaks":
        self._reconstruct_y_peaks(md)
    # Always invalidate heatmap cache
    self.clear_map_cache_requested.emit(md.name)

docs.title: _post_bulk_action(apply_all, action)
docs.text: Called once after all MapData objects have been processed. The Maps override refreshes fit results and re-emits the map view.

docs.title: _emit_selected_spectra() Override
docs.text:
The Maps override builds a "type": "tensor" payload (shared x-axis batch) instead of the Spectra workspace's "type": "tensor_list" (independent arrays per spectrum):

# Maps workspace:
batch_data = {
    'type': 'tensor',
    'x': x,             # shared float64[M_proc]
    'y': Y,             # float32[n_selected, M_proc]
    'indices': indices, # which rows within the map
    ...
}

This lets VSpectraViewer render multiple map spectra using matrix operations rather than a Python loop.

docs.title: Maps → Spectra Workspace
docs.text:
# User selects spectra in Maps workspace and clicks "Send to Spectra"
vm.send_selected_spectra_to_spectra_workspace()

For each selected spectrum:

  1. Builds a deep-copied payload dict (raw x0, Y0, baseline_config, fit_model, range_min/max, is_subtracted).
  2. Emits send_spectra_to_workspace(payloads).
  3. main.py connects that signal to the Spectra ViewModel's receive_spectra(), which registers each payload as a new N=1 MapData block in the Spectra workspace's SpectraStore.

Deep copying prevents cross-workspace state pollution — editing the spectrum in the Spectra tab does not affect the original map.

docs.title: Maps → Graphs Workspace (Profile Extraction)
docs.text:
When the user selects exactly 2 points in 2D map mode and clicks "Extract profile":

  1. User Action: The user selects exactly 2 points on a 2D map and clicks "Extract profile".
  2. View → ViewModel: VMapViewer signals extract_profile_requested(profile_name).
  3. Extraction Logic: VWorkspaceMaps delegates to _extract_profile(), which constructs a profile_df dataframe by interpolating points along the line segment.
  4. Forwarding Payload: The View passes the payload to VMWorkspaceMaps.extract_and_send_profile_to_graphs().
  5. Workspace Transfer: The ViewModel directly invokes VMWorkspaceGraphs.add_dataframe().
  6. UI Update: A signal instructs the main window to switch focus to the Graphs tab.

The profile DataFrame has columns distance (µm) and values (Z intensity). The Graphs workspace auto-creates a line plot from it.

docs.title: Fit Results with Spatial Columns
docs.text:
collect_fit_results() overrides the parent to add spatial and zone columns:

# After super().collect_fit_results():
# base DataFrame includes: Filename, X, Y, [Quadrant, Zone for wafers],
# sorted fit parameters (x0_Peak1, fwhm_Peak1, area_Peak1, ...), and trailing R2

# Maps workspace adds X, Y, and ensures Quadrant and Zone are present for wafer maps

# Final columns:
# Filename | X | Y | Quadrant | Zone | x0_Peak1 | fwhm_Peak1 | area_Peak1 | ... | R2

Zone classifies by radial distance:

Zone Distance Center ≤ 35 % of radius Mid-Radius 35 – 80 % Edge ≥ 80 %

Quadrant classifies by sign of (X, Y): Q1 (−,−), Q2 (−,+), Q3 (+,+), Q4 (+,−).

docs.title: Modern Format (v2+, ZIP-backed)
docs.text:
Maps workspace files (.maps) use the same ZIP structure described in SpectraStore: Persistence, with heavier content due to larger tensors.

Map DataFrames are serialized with a custom binary format for speed:

# Fast serialization (vs to_csv which is 20-70× slower)
arr = map_df.to_numpy()
buf = io.BytesIO(); np.save(buf, arr)
gzip.compress(buf.getvalue(), compresslevel=1)  # level=1: 70× faster, ~5% larger

docs.title: Legacy Loader
docs.text:
_load_legacy_maps() handles old .maps JSON files where each map was stored as a gzip+hex CSV string:

  1. Parses the top-level "maps" dict (map_name → hex_string).
  2. Decompresses and reads each CSV into a DataFrame.
  3. Builds a coordinate lookup dict from the "spectrums_data" entries (keyed by (map_name, x, y)).
  4. Registers each map into SpectraStore via add_map().
  5. Vectorized-restores baselines, peak curves, and fit results.

docs.title: Adding a New Map File Format
docs.text:
1. Create a loader function in spectroview/model/io/m_io.py (e.g., load_xyz_map(path) → pd.DataFrame).
  2. In VMWorkspaceMaps.load_map_files(), add an elif path.suffix.lower() == '.xyz': branch.
  3. The returned DataFrame must have X and Y columns followed by numeric wavenumber columns.
  4. If the format provides metadata, return a (DataFrame, dict) tuple and store the dict in self.maps_metadata[map_name].

docs.title: Adding a New Z-Parameter Type
docs.text:
New Z-parameter types are computed in VMapViewer._compute_z_values(). To add, e.g., a peak ratio:

  1. Add the parameter name to the VMapViewer combobox population logic.
  2. In _compute_z_values(), add an elif parameter == "My Ratio": branch that reads from df_fit_results.
  3. The cache key already includes parameter, so caching works automatically.

docs.title: Adding a New Map Type (beyond Wafer)
docs.text:
New spatial layouts require:

  1. Add the type string to the cbb_map_type combobox.
  2. In VMapViewer.plot_heatmap(), add a rendering branch (likely scipy.griddata with a custom mask).
  3. In VMWorkspaceMaps.collect_fit_results(), add a zone/quadrant classification branch for the new type.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Heatmap does not update after fitting

  • collect_fit_results() must be called after _on_fit_finished(). Check that clear_map_cache_requested is emitted for the map name, and that the cache key's parameter matches what is currently selected in the combobox.

Selected pixel does not highlight the correct spectrum

  • The mapping from (x, y) coordinates to fnames relies on the format {map_name}_(x, y) matching md.fnames. Check that float(x_pos) renders the same string in _extract_spectra_from_map() and in _on_map_viewer_selection().

Fitting a large map freezes the UI briefly at start

  • Task construction (_run_fit_thread()) happens on the main thread before VBFthread.start(). For very large maps, the np.arange(md.n_spectra) index build is fast, but the vstack of Y matrices can be slow. Profile the _run_fit_thread() call with cProfile if this becomes a bottleneck.

Send to Spectra creates duplicate spectra

  • The Spectra ViewModel's receive_spectra() checks name in self.store.map_names before adding. If duplicates appear, check that the fname format is consistent (watch for floating-point rounding in (x_pos, y_pos) string representations).

Wafer griddata is slow on every redraw

  • Ensure clear_map_cache_requested is only emitted when necessary (after fitting, not on every selection change). Check that the cache_key tuple is hashable and stable — if any element changes inadvertently between renders, the cache will never hit.

Memory spike when loading many large maps

  • For a 50×50 map (2,500 spectra) at 1,000 wavenumbers, MapData.Y0 (float32) is ~10 MB; for a 25,000-spectrum map at 1,000 wavenumbers, Y0 is ~100 MB, and fitting allocates additional arrays (Y_bestfit and one Y_peaks entry per peak). Use remove_map() for maps no longer needed.

For data-model troubleshooting (preprocessing not applied, memory management), see SpectraStore: Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Local MCP Server
docs.text: SPECTROview can expose the state of the currently running desktop application to trusted MCP clients on the same computer. The server is disabled by default, binds only to 127.0.0.1, and uses MCP Streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp unless another port is selected.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    GUI[PySide6 GUI] --> VM[Workspace ViewModels]
    CHAT[Existing AI Chat] --> CTX[Chat snapshot context]
    CTX --> TOOLS[Shared FastMCP tool definitions]
    CHAT --> CMD[Typed graph commands]
    CMD --> API[SpectroviewApplicationAPI]
    HTTP[Local MCP Streamable HTTP] --> TOOLS
    TOOLS --> API
    API --> DISPATCH[Qt main-thread dispatcher]
    DISPATCH --> VM
    VM --> STORE[SpectraStore / MGraph / VBF engine]

There are two related APIs:

  • spectroview.api creates independent headless workspaces for Python scripts.
  • spectroview.application.SpectroviewApplicationAPI controls the currently running desktop session. It is the live application boundary used by MCP.

The MCP layer contains no fitting, preprocessing, or rendering algorithm. It uses the existing ViewModel orchestration, SpectraStore, graph_control, and Vectorized Batch Fit engine. Graph rendering remains a View responsibility.

docs.title: Why embedded Streamable HTTP
docs.text:
Three runtime designs were considered:

Design Result Embedded server in the desktop process Selected. It has direct access to the current state and needs only one Qt dispatch boundary. Separate localhost service with custom IPC Rejected for the first iteration. It adds another protocol, state synchronization, and lifecycle failure mode. Separate stdio MCP process plus IPC bridge Rejected for live desktop state. Stdio is useful when the client owns the server process, but the SPECTROview GUI is already the state owner.

Streamable HTTP is used instead of the superseded SSE transport. Uvicorn runs on a daemon thread; LocalMCPRuntime.stop() provides deterministic shutdown. The FastMCP ASGI application retains the SDK's localhost Host/Origin checks.

docs.title: Enable and connect
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → AI → Local MCP Server.
  2. Check Enable local MCP endpoint.
  3. Keep the default port or choose an unused port from 1024 to 65535.
  4. Select OK. The endpoint starts immediately; no application restart is required.
  5. Configure an MCP client with the displayed Streamable HTTP URL, normally:
http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp

The SPECTROview desktop application must be running. Disabling the setting or closing SPECTROview stops the endpoint.

docs.title: Security and permissions
docs.text:
• The bind address is hard-coded to IPv4 loopback and is not editable in the UI. SPECTROview does not listen on a LAN/public interface.
  • There is no authentication in this loopback-only first iteration. Do not proxy or port-forward the endpoint.
  • Read and write tools are distinct and their descriptions identify mutations.
  • MCP read_only_hint, destructive_hint, idempotent_hint, and open_world_hint annotations classify tools for clients that implement approval policies.
  • export_results requires a caller-supplied path, never creates a parent directory, and refuses to replace an existing file unless the call includes overwrite=true.
  • Dataset or graph deletion is never inferred from a read request. delete_graph is an explicit state-changing tool.

This separation gives a future Work Harness enough information to apply an approval policy to graph changes, processing, fitting, deletion, and exports.

docs.title: Tools
Resources
docs.text:
URI Contents spectroview://application/state Application/workspace summary spectroview://workspace/current Current workspace and selection spectroview://datasets Compact loaded-dataset catalog spectroview://dataframes/detail DataFrame columns, samples, preview spectroview://graphs/detail All graph configurations spectroview://graphs/current Active graph configuration or typed error spectroview://fit/current Active fit configuration or typed error

Resources are read-only context. Actions remain tools.

docs.title: Thread safety
docs.text:
The HTTP/ASGI thread never reads or mutates Qt-owned state directly. QtMainThreadDispatcher emits a queued signal carrying a callable and waits on the server thread for its result. The callable executes on the QApplication thread. Calls already on that thread execute directly. Requests during shutdown fail with APPLICATION_NOT_READY; stalled dispatches fail with MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT rather than waiting forever.

Fitting itself remains asynchronous and continues to use SPECTROview's existing VBFthread. fit_spectrum reports that the fit started; clients inspect get_application_state before collecting results.

docs.title: Existing AI Chat compatibility
docs.text:
The internal chat is not converted into an HTTP client. Its existing MCP hub, ReAct loop, provider adapters, conversation behavior, and typed graph-command queue are unchanged. It intentionally keeps the original compact five-tool profile (query_dataframe, get_statistics, plot_graph, update_graph, delete_graph) because large schemas materially reduce small local model reliability. The resulting graph commands are applied through SpectroviewApplicationAPI, the same live application boundary used by the external server.

The chat's DataFrame and graph reads remain turn snapshots. Routing a synchronous in-process chat tool call back through a blocking Qt dispatcher would deadlock the GUI thread; the external server does not have that constraint.

docs.title: Adding a capability
docs.text:
1. Reuse or add a domain operation in a Model/ViewModel or the headless spectroview.api; do not implement scientific logic in the MCP handler.
  2. Add a domain-shaped method to SpectroviewApplicationAPI. Keep widget lookup, combo boxes, dialogs, and signal wiring inside the adapter.
  3. Register a typed tool in create_mcp_server(..., include_application_tools=True). Use Literal/Field constraints and the {ok,result|error} response envelope.
  4. Decide explicitly whether it is read-only, state-changing, destructive, or a filesystem write. Require an overwrite/delete flag where appropriate.
  5. Add service tests, generated-schema tests, valid/invalid MCP calls, and a thread-boundary test if Qt state is touched.
  6. Update the tool/resource tables on this page.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Connection refused: enable the server, keep SPECTROview running, and use the exact endpoint displayed in Settings.
  • Server failed / port in use: select another port and press OK. The status bar reports startup failures.
  • HTTP 421: connect with 127.0.0.1 or localhost. The SDK intentionally rejects unexpected Host headers to reduce DNS-rebinding risk.
  • APPLICATION_NOT_READY: SPECTROview is starting/stopping, or the compact internal-chat profile was used without a live desktop facade.
  • MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT: a modal dialog or long GUI operation prevented the main event loop from servicing the request. Close the dialog and retry.
  • No fit results: wait for fitting to finish, then call get_fit_results with collect=true once before exporting.

docs.title: Intentional first-iteration limits
docs.text:
• No graph-image export tool yet; only fit-result export is exposed.
  • No smoothing tool is exposed because no single supported workspace operation currently owns a stable smoothing contract.
  • MCP cannot create/edit fit models or baseline points yet; it can inspect a configured model and run the existing engine.
  • Map colormap/viewer customization and map image export are not exposed.
  • No authentication, remote bind, TLS, server-initiated sampling, or elicitation.
  • No MCP progress notifications for VBF; fit progress is currently polled from application state.

docs.title: Multivariate Analysis (MVA) of Raman Spectroscopic Data
docs.text: This document provides a technical overview of the Multivariate Analysis (MVA) features implemented in SPECTROview.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The MVA feature follows the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) architectural pattern:

  • Model (spectroview/model/analysis/m_mva.py): Contains the core mathematics for MVA techniques, specifically Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF). Uses standard numerical libraries (numpy, scipy) without requiring extra dependencies like scikit-learn.
  • ViewModel (spectroview/viewmodel/analysis/vm_mva.py): Orchestrates the data flow. It extracts preprocessed data from active spectra, invokes the Model to perform calculations, caches results, and computes per-spectrum reconstruction errors.
  • View (spectroview/view/components/lower_tabs/: v_mva.py, v_mva_plots.py): Provides the user interface with a tabbed plot panel (Summary, Scree Plot, Loadings, Heatmap, Scores, Residuals), interactive parameter controls, and matplotlib navigation toolbars for each plot.

docs.title: Algorithm Implementation
docs.text: The PCA implementation in SPECTROview uses Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on mean-centered data.

docs.title: Visualization Enhancements
docs.text:
SPECTROview features a comprehensive tabbed plot interface for visualizing results:

  • Summary: 2×2 dashboard showing Scree Plot (PCA only), first 3 Loadings, and primary Score scatter projections
  • Scree Plot (PCA only): Bar chart of individual variance + cumulative line
  • Loadings: Spectral loading overlays with fill-between for visual clarity
  • Heatmap: 2D spatial map of selected component scores when spectrum names carry (x, y) coordinates
  • Scores: 2D scatter with interactive axis selection
  • Residuals: Per-spectrum reconstruction error for model quality assessment

docs.title: 1. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
docs.text:
PCA is a dimensionality reduction technique that transforms spectra into a new coordinate system such that the greatest variance by any projection of the data lies on the first coordinate (the first principal component).

  • Implementation Details: Implemented using Singular Value Decomposition (numpy.linalg.svd) on optionally mean-centered data.
  • Parameters:
  • Components: Number of principal components to retain (2–50).
  • Mean centering: Whether to subtract the mean spectrum before SVD (default: on). This is standard practice for spectral PCA.
  • Visualizations:
  • Summary: 2×2 overview dashboard combining top Scree, Loadings, and Score pairs.
  • Scree Plot: Displays the percentage of variance explained by each principal component and the cumulative variance.
  • Loadings: Visualizes the spectral contribution to each principal component, with percentage of explained variance in the legend.
  • Heatmap: 2D spatial score plot for a selectable component when (x, y) coordinates are encoded in spectrum names.
  • Scores: Provides a 2D scatter plot of the spectra projected onto the principal components, with interactive axis selection.
  • Residuals: Per-spectrum L2 reconstruction error for model quality assessment.

docs.title: 2. Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF)
docs.text:
NMF factors the data matrix into two non-negative matrices (typically W and H). This is particularly useful for spectroscopic data, as it yields additive, non-negative components that often correspond to physical endmembers.

  • Implementation Details: Uses the Lee & Seung multiplicative update rules. It iteratively updates the matrices to minimize the Frobenius norm of the reconstruction error.
  • Parameters:
  • Components: The number of non-negative components (or endmembers) to extract from the dataset.
  • Max Iterations: The maximum number of multiplicative update iterations the algorithm is allowed to perform. If the algorithm does not converge within this limit, it will stop.
  • Tolerance: The convergence threshold. The algorithm stops early if the relative change in the reconstruction error between successive iterations falls below this value.
  • Random Seed: A seed value for the random number generator used to initialize the matrices. Setting a fixed seed ensures that the NMF results are reproducible across runs (default: 42).
  • Visualizations:
  • Summary: Overview dashboard of Loadings and primary NMF score projections.
  • Loadings: Displays the non-negative spectral components (endmembers).
  • Heatmap: 2D spatial abundance map for a selectable NMF component when (x, y) coordinates are present in spectrum names.
  • Scores: Provides a 2D scatter plot of the concentration/abundances of these components across the dataset.
  • Residuals: Per-spectrum L2 reconstruction error.

Why doesn't NMF have a Scree Plot? Unlike PCA, which strictly orders orthogonal components by the maximum variance they explain, NMF finds non-orthogonal, additive components (endmembers) that mix together. Because NMF components are not orthogonal and are not sequentially ordered by variance, an isolated percentage of "variance explained" cannot be calculated for each individual component. To evaluate an NMF model, rely on the Residuals plot to assess reconstruction quality, and the Loadings to ensure components correspond to physically meaningful spectra.

docs.title: User Interface
docs.text: The MVA view uses a split-panel layout:

docs.title: Left Panel (Controls)
docs.text:
• Method Selection: Radio buttons to switch between PCA and NMF.
  • Parameter Groups: Separate group boxes for PCA and NMF parameters, showing only the relevant parameters for the selected method.
  • Run Button: Executes the analysis.
  • Export Section: Sends scores to the Graphs workspace.

docs.title: Right Panel (Tabbed Plots)
docs.text:
Each plot type occupies its own tab in a QTabWidget:

  • Summary: Combined overview grid (Scree Plot [PCA], first 3 Loadings, and primary Score scatter projections).
  • Scree Plot (PCA only): Variance explained per component.
  • Loadings: Spectral loading profiles.
  • Heatmap: 2D spatial map of selected component scores (requires (x, y) coordinates in spectrum names).
  • Scores: Interactive 2D scatter with axis selection.
  • Residuals: Per-spectrum reconstruction quality.

Each tab includes a matplotlib NavigationToolbar for zoom, pan, and save operations.

docs.title: Data Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Selection: MVA operates exclusively on the active (checked) spectra in the SPECTROview workspace.
  2. Preprocessing: VMMVA pulls data directly from SpectraStore (md.Y when preprocessed, falling back to md.Y0 when raw), meaning it operates on data that has already undergone user-configured preprocessing steps (baseline subtraction, cropping, X-correction).
  3. Interpolation: If the selected spectra have varying wavenumber axes, they are automatically interpolated onto a common grid (the grid of the first active spectrum) to build a consistent data matrix.
  4. Export: The results (scores for PCA, W matrix for NMF) can be exported directly to the Graphs workspace for further visualization and comparison.

docs.title: Citations and References
docs.text:
If these features are used to generate results for publication, users are kindly requested to cite the relevant literature for the implemented algorithms:

[1] PCA algorithm: Wold, S., Esbensen, K., and Geladi, P., "Principal component analysis." Chemometrics and intelligent laboratory systems 2.1-3 (1987): 37-52.

[2] NMF algorithm: Lee, Daniel D., and H. Sebastian Seung, "Learning the parts of objects by non-negative matrix factorization." Nature 401.6755 (1999): 788-791.

docs.title: Workspace: Spectra
docs.text:
The Spectra workspace is the core analytical environment for individual spectrum management. It handles loading, preprocessing, peak modeling, fitting, and exporting spectral data. It also serves as the base class that the Maps workspace extends via inheritance.

[!NOTE] This page covers the Spectra-specific View and ViewModel layers. For the shared data model (SpectraStore, MapData, MapInfo, proxies), see the dedicated Data Architecture: SpectraStore page.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The workspace follows a strict MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) separation. No layer may cross its boundary in the wrong direction.

graph LR
    subgraph View ["View Layer (v_*)"]
        VWS["VWorkspaceSpectra<br/>(QWidget)"]
        SV["VSpectraViewer<br/>(Matplotlib canvas)"]
        SLE["SpectraLegendEditorDialog<br/>(batch legend editor)"]
        FMB["VFitModelBuilder<br/>(controls panel)"]
        PT["VPeakTable<br/>(parameter table)"]
        SL["VSpectraList<br/>(QListView)"]
        FR["VFitResults<br/>(results table)"]
        MVA["VMVA<br/>(PCA/NMF panel)"]
    end

    subgraph VM ["ViewModel Layer (vm_*)"]
        VMWS["VMWorkspaceSpectra<br/>(QObject)"]
        VMFMB["VMFitModelBuilder"]
        VMMVA["VMMVA"]
    end

    subgraph Model ["Model Layer"]
        SS["SpectraStore"]
        IO["m_io<br/>(file loaders)"]
        VBF["VBFthread<br/>(fit engine)"]
        WIO["WorkspaceIO<br/>(serialization)"]
    end

    VWS --> SV & FMB & SL & FR & MVA
    SV --> SLE
    VWS -->|"method calls"| VMWS
    VMWS -->|"Qt signals"| VWS
    VMWS --> SS & IO & VBF & WIO
    VMWS --> VMFMB & VMMVA

docs.title: Component Responsibilities
docs.text: Layer Class Responsibility View VWorkspaceSpectra Assembles UI widgets, connects signals/slots, delegates all logic to ViewModel View VSpectraViewer Matplotlib canvas — renders 1D spectra, baselines, peaks, best-fit, residuals, 2D heatmaps, interactive 3D views, and range selectors View VRangeSelectorPanel Vertical right-side panel with red, blue, and green toggle buttons for spectral intervals View RangeSelectorManager Canvas overlay managing draggable bracket markers and shaded spans for active selectors View VLiveMaps Live Maps tab hosting three synchronized 2D heatmap subpanels (Red, Blue, Green) View SpectraLegendEditorDialog Transactional palette, legend-limit, label, and color editor for selected spectra View VFitModelBuilder X-correction, range, baseline and fit controls panel View VPeakTable Editable table of peak parameters with per-row model selectors View VSpectraList Checkbox list with coloring rules, drag-to-reorder, multi-select ViewModel VMWorkspaceSpectra Business logic: orchestrates loading, preprocessing, fitting, persistence ViewModel VMLiveMaps Computes 2D spatial parameter arrays from MapData on selector interval/parameter updates Model spectral_parameters Vectorized calculations for integrated/mean/max intensity, peak position, height, and area Model SpectraStore Tensor-centric in-memory store — see spectra_store.md Model VBFthread QThread that runs the vectorized batch fitting engine off the main thread

docs.title: How Spectra Uses MapData
docs.text: In the Spectra workspace, each loaded spectrum is stored as an independent MapData block with N=1 (one row). Each block has its own x-axis, allowing spectra with different wavenumber ranges to coexist. See Data Hierarchy for the full tensor layout.

docs.title: VWorkspaceSpectra — The View Coordinator
docs.text:
File: v_workspace_spectra.py

VWorkspaceSpectra is a pure UI assembly class. It:

  1. Instantiates all child widgets and the ViewModel in __init__.
  2. Wires every signal/slot connection in setup_connections().
  3. Delegates every user action to the ViewModel (never manipulates data directly).
  4. Updates UI in response to ViewModel signals.

The layout is a horizontal splitter: left (SpectraViewer on top, tabbed controls below) and right (spectra list sidebar).

Key pattern — Ctrl-modified actions:

def _apply_with_ctrl(self, fn):
    apply_all = bool(QApplication.keyboardModifiers() & Qt.ControlModifier)
    fn(apply_all)

# Usage:
self.btn_reinit.clicked.connect(lambda: self._apply_with_ctrl(vm.reinit_spectra))

All bulk actions (baseline subtract, peak paste, reinit, fit) follow this pattern. A normal click applies to selected spectra; Ctrl+click applies to all spectra in the store.

docs.title: VSpectraViewer — 2D Heatmap Mode
docs.text:
Package: spectra_viewer/ (v_plot_heatmap.py)

VSpectraViewer is the core spectral canvas widget. In addition to multi-line 1D spectrum visualization, it provides a native 2D Heatmap Mode (btn_heatmap, located alongside btn_3d on the right side of the toolbar directly to the left of btn_options / btn_copy) for visualizing series data (e.g., temperature variations, kinetics, line scans):

  • Data Alignment & Ragged Matrix Interpolation: When selected spectra possess differing or ragged wavenumber grids, _plot_heatmap() aligns all rows onto a common spectral range via scipy.interpolate.interp1d.
  • Y-Axis Token Extraction: Automatically parses numeric parameters embedded in filenames (e.g. _100C_, _250K_) using regex tokenization, or defaults to index-based ordering (0..N-1).
  • Smooth Vertical Interpolation: Supports 1D cubic/linear interpolation along the vertical axis when spin_heatmap_interp > 0 (default 300 points).
  • Dynamic Toolbar Adaptation: Activating heatmap mode toggles toolbar state: standard 1D tools (btn_peak, btn_baseline, btn_eraser, btn_norm, btn_bestfit, and shift_panel) are hidden via setVisible(False), while heatmap-specific controls (cbb_heatmap_yaxis, le_heatmap_ylabel, spin_heatmap_interp) become visible. Unchecking the mode restores the 1D tools immediately.

docs.title: VSpectraViewer — Interactive 3D View Mode
docs.text:
VSpectraViewer provides an interactive 3D View (btn_3d, _3d_mode) built directly on Matplotlib's mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.Axes3D (_plot_3d()), keeping zero external dependencies and sharing PLOT_POLICY_LIGHT/PLOT_POLICY_DARK styling, clipboard figure export, and workspace option synchronization (view_3d in get_options_state()/set_options_state()):

  • Projection Switching & Callback Cleanup (_ensure_axes_projection): Switches self.ax between 2D rectilinear axes and Axes3D only when changing into or out of 3D mode, disconnecting Axes3D canvas callbacks and disabling 3D mouse bindings before figure.delaxes() to prevent callback accumulation across mode switches.
  • Vectorized 3D Rendering (FastLine3DCollection): Subclasses Line3DCollection to project all 3D points across uniform (N, M, 3) tensors or ragged tensor_list selections in a single vectorized proj3d._proj_trans_points() pass and updates Path._vertices in place during interactive camera rotation, supporting "line" and "dot" plot styles, normalization, raw overlays, best-fit curves, Z-log scaling, and legend/colorbar modes.
  • Mouse Rotation & Mode Exclusivity (_sync_mode_toolbar_state): btn_3d and btn_heatmap are mutually exclusive. Activating 3D mode automatically turns off NoDoubleClickZoomToolbar 2D zoom (_set_zoom_tool_active(False)), hides incompatible 1D tools (btn_zoom, btn_peak, btn_baseline, btn_eraser, shift_panel), and shares cbb_heatmap_yaxis / le_heatmap_ylabel for filename-token Y-axis positioning so left-drag rotates (elev, azim), middle-drag pans, right-drag or scroll scales Z, and Rescale (Ctrl+R) resets camera angles (25°, -60°) and data bounds.

docs.title: Interactive Spectral Mapping & Live Maps
docs.text:
The interactive spectral mapping subsystem allows users to select up to three independent spectral ranges on the 1D spectrum viewer and see live-updating parameter visualizations in real time:

  • Spectra Workspace (mode="spectra"): Renders up to three color-coded (Red, Blue, Green) 1D trend curves (Spectrum # vs. parameter value) across the currently selected spectra in VSpectraList.
  • Maps Workspace (mode="map"): Automatically adapts to the dimensionality of the selected map: renders 2D spatial parameter heatmaps for 2D maps, or 1D line plots along the spatial coordinate (X (mm), Y (mm), or Distance (mm)) for 1D profile maps (line scans).
  • Red/Blue Ratio (R/B ratio): Available in the Green channel subpanel across both workspaces; computes the element-wise integrated intensity ratio \(I_{\mathrm{Red}} / I_{\mathrm{Blue}}\) with NaN masking for zero/near-zero Blue intensities and updates automatically when Red or Blue brackets move. While R/B ratio is selected, the Green bracket is hidden on VSpectraViewer so only the Red and Blue brackets driving the ratio remain visible.
graph TD
    subgraph Spectra Viewer
        RP["VRangeSelectorPanel<br/>(Red, Blue, Green toggle buttons)"]
        RSM["RangeSelectorManager<br/>(Interactive brackets & shaded spans)"]
    end

    subgraph ViewModel
        VMLM["VMLiveMaps<br/>(60 ms debounce timer, mode='spectra' | 'map')"]
    end

    subgraph Model
        SP["spectral_parameters.py<br/>(Vectorized numpy parameter calculation)"]
    end

    subgraph Live Maps Tab
        VLM["VLiveMaps<br/>(Tab placed immediately before More)"]
        Sub["LiveMapSubpanel x 3<br/>(1D Series Curve in Spectra / 2D Heatmap in Maps)"]
    end

    RP -->|"range_toggled(key, active)"| RSM & VMLM
    RSM -->|"range_changed(key, xmin, xmax)"| VMLM
    VMLM -->|"compute_spectral_parameter() /<br/>compute_series_spectral_parameter()"| SP
    VMLM -->|"series_data_ready / map_data_ready"| VLM
    VLM --> Sub
  • VRangeSelectorPanel & SpectraRangeBracketMixin (rgb_live_maps/v_range_selector.py, v_range_bracket_mixin.py): VRangeSelectorPanel is positioned as a dedicated vertical panel on the right side of VSpectraViewer with Red (#e74c3c), Blue (#3498db), and Green (#2ecc71) toggle buttons. SpectraRangeBracketMixin wires the panel, range initialization/clamping, hover cursor feedback, and Agg background blitting directly into VSpectraViewer.
  • RangeSelectorManager: Manages interactive vertical boundary lines, inward bracket annotations, and transparent spans for each selector, reusing existing artists in-place across drags and supporting set_animated(True) / active_artists(). Tracks per-channel parameter selection via set_parameter() / is_bracket_visible(), hiding and disabling hit-testing for the Green bracket whenever its Live Maps panel displays R/B ratio (restoring it immediately when another spectral parameter is selected). Dragging either line or the center span translates or resizes the interval via Agg background blitting (temporary layout_engine suspension, hover-peak bypass while dragging, and X-clamping outside vertical axes bounds), while emitting range_drag_finished on mouse release. Hit testing uses pixel tolerance with coordinate translation from Matplotlib transforms.
  • VMLiveMaps: Owns selector intervals, parameter selections, colormap choices, and mode ("spectra" or "map"). Uses an adaptive debounce timer (baseline 60 ms, scaling up to 250 ms on very large maps) during continuous dragging, flushes queued ranges immediately on release via flush_pending(), and automatically offloads map batches with >= 25,000 spectra (ASYNC_SPECTRUM_THRESHOLD) to a QThreadPool QRunnable (_LiveMapWorker) guarded by monotonic _generation_id stale cancellation and clean shutdown(). In "spectra" mode, set_series_data(mds) preserves user-adjusted bracket positions across spectrum selection changes when within axis bounds, emits spatial_sites_changed(None), and emits series_data_ready. In "map" mode, set_map_datas(mds, primary_name) enforces signature deduplication and MapData.data_version LRU result caching, excludes inactive (~is_active) spectra, caches regular/Delaunay MapGridder geometry, emits spatial_sites_changed with ordered active coordinates/profile positions for interactive selection, and emits map_data_ready, profile_data_ready, multi_profile_data_ready, map_2d_candidates_changed, or live_maps_cleared. Both workspaces skip Live Maps computation while the Live Maps tab is hidden (_live_maps_dirty), flushing once when the user opens the tab.
  • spectral_parameters.py: Model-level vectorized evaluation over slice-before-cast MapData.y_matrix[:, mask] views via compute_spectral_parameter() (with optional active_mask), across discrete selected spectra (list[MapData]) via compute_series_spectral_parameter(), map dimensionality detection via analyze_map_geometry(), reusable regular/Delaunay barycentric gridding via build_map_gridder() + compute_map_grid(), and safe element-wise ratio computation with relative epsilon NaN masking via compute_intensity_ratio(). Calculates:
  • Direct: Integrated intensity, Mean intensity, Maximum intensity, Peak position, Peak height (baseline-subtracted).
  • Derived (Green channel): R/B ratio (\(I_{\mathrm{Red}} / I_{\mathrm{Blue}}\)).
  • Fitted: Peak position (fit), Peak height (fit), Peak area (fit) using fitted peak parameters when available.
  • VLiveMaps & LiveMapSubpanel (rgb_live_maps/): QWidget tab installed in bottom_tabs (between Fit Results and MVA, with More placed at the end of the tabs). Hosts a top toolbar row combining a contextual left strip ([◀ | ComboBox | ▶] 2D map switcher and diagnostic notices — hidden when unused) with persistent right-aligned Show Legend and compact 2-column More view options controls (btn_legend, btn_options, (2, 2, 2, 2) row margins matching VSpectraViewer), plus 3 independent subpanels (LiveMapSubpanel in v_live_map_subpanel.py, 96 DPI baseline) featuring per-panel Rescale, Pan, and Zoom buttons synced to NoDoubleClickZoomToolbar (preserving legend double-click editing), size-invariant figure clipboard copy (Copied figure size default 5.5 × 4.0 in & Copied figure theme), and Ctrl + Click TSV data copy via copy_data_requested(color_id) / copy_df_to_clb() (copying spectrum index/labels + parameter values in "spectra" mode, 1D/multi-profile tables, or 2D (X, Y, Value) site data via VMLiveMaps.get_2d_copy_points()). In mode="map", LiveMapSubpanel reuses shared map_selection.py helpers (MapCanvasSelector, resolve_xy_selection(), resolve_1d_profile_selection()) to provide click, Ctrl+Click, and marquee-drag spectrum selection across R/B/G plots when Pan/Zoom and legend hits are inactive, emitting VLiveMaps.spectra_selected back to VWorkspaceMaps while keeping interactive XY selection disabled in mode="spectra".
