View options default to plot_theme="Light Mode" (independent of Qt UI theme via apply_global_theme()), plot_style="line", line_width=1.5, dot_size=1.5, show_figure_label=False, and show_grid=False, persist across restarts in MSettings (live_maps_view_options/*, cross-synced across Spectra & Maps workspaces), and use apply_view_options_fast(), @lru_cache mplstyle dicts (_get_cached_style_dict), settled-layout freezing (_on_canvas_draw), and parented 35 ms redraw timers for stall-free X/Y/Z scale, style, text size (6–24 pt), figure title label, gridline, shared-Y, heatmap smoothing, colorbar, and legend-editor updates backed by v_live_maps_legend_editor.py.
  • Zoom & Range Coordination: When a range selector is activated, btn_zoom is automatically deactivated so bracket adjustment can occur without triggering simultaneous zoom rectangles, and VWorkspaceSpectra._on_range_selector_toggled() automatically switches bottom_tabs to self.v_live_maps (flushing any deferred _live_maps_dirty selection before calculating the activated channel; deactivating a selector leaves the active tab unchanged). The Zoom button can also be toggled off by clicking it, and while Zoom is active, clicking inside the range span performs a zoom rather than moving the range body.

docs.title: VMWorkspaceSpectra — The ViewModel
docs.text:
File: vm_workspace_spectra.py (composed with vm_spectra_preprocessing.py, vm_spectra_fitting.py, vm_spectra_results.py, and vm_spectra_persistence.py)

This is the largest and most critical class in the application. It owns the SpectraStore and orchestrates every operation.

docs.title: Template Method Hooks
docs.text:
The ViewModel uses the Template Method pattern to allow the Maps subclass to customize bulk operations without duplicating the operation logic:

def _get_target_mds(self, apply_all: bool) -> list[MapData]:
    """Which MapData blocks to operate on."""
    # Spectra workspace: selected spectra → their MapData objects
    # Maps workspace (override): the current map, or all maps

def _on_map_data_changed(self, md: MapData, action: str):
    """Hook after each individual MapData is modified."""
    # Spectra workspace: no-op
    # Maps workspace (override): clears heatmap cache, re-runs batch_preprocess

def _post_bulk_action(self, apply_all: bool, action: str):
    """Hook after all target MapData objects have been processed."""
    # Spectra workspace: re-emits list and selection
    # Maps workspace (override): also refreshes fit results and map view

docs.title: VSpectraViewer — The Plot Canvas
docs.text:
Package: spectra_viewer/ (v_spectra_viewer.py, v_spectra_options.py, v_plot_1d.py, v_plot_heatmap.py, v_plot_3d.py, v_interactions.py, v_spectra_legend_editor.py, common.py)

VSpectraViewer composes dedicated mixins over QWidget (SpectraOptionsMenuMixin, SpectraPlot1DMixin, SpectraHeatmapMixin, SpectraPlot3DMixin, SpectraLegendMixin, SpectraInteractionMixin, and SpectraRangeBracketMixin), separating the 2-column options menu and state sync, 1D/heatmap/3D rendering, mouse/peak/eraser interactions, and legend/colorbar management while keeping shared helpers in common.py.

The Matplotlib canvas renders everything visible in the spectrum plot. It receives a data dictionary from VMWorkspaceSpectra.spectra_selection_changed and redraws accordingly.

Rendered elements:

Element Source data key Spectrum lines data["y"] (processed) Raw overlay (optional) data["y0"] (raw) Baseline curve data["y_baseline"] Baseline anchor points data["baseline_config"]["points"] Individual peak curves data["y_peaks"] (list of arrays) Best-fit envelope data["y_bestfit"] Residuals data["y"] - data["y_bestfit"] R² annotation data["fit_r2"][0]

Interaction modes (radio button exclusive):

Mode Left click Right click Zoom Standard Matplotlib zoom/pan — Baseline Add anchor point at x Remove nearest anchor Peak Add peak at x Remove nearest peak

Peaks can also be dragged. The viewer emits peak_dragged(x, y) during drag and peak_drag_finished() on release, which the ViewModel translates into update_dragged_peak() + finalize_peak_drag() calls.

docs.title: Batch Legend Editing
docs.text:
VSpectraViewer caches the complete legend bounding box after rendering. A double-click anywhere within that box opens SpectraLegendEditorDialog from spectra_viewer/v_spectra_legend_editor.py; individual legend handles and text objects no longer launch separate editors.

The dialog is transactional: its palette selector, legend-limit spinbox, label fields, and color comboboxes hold temporary values until the user accepts it. Cancel therefore causes no mutation. On OK, VSpectraViewer._apply_legend_editor_values():

  1. Updates the shared color_palette and max_legend_items view options.
  2. Writes changed labels and explicit colors to the current tensor payload.
  3. Writes the same values through each SpectrumProxy, updating the source MapData.labels and MapData.colors arrays.
  4. Emits spectrumCustomized, causing the ViewModel to rebuild the selection payload and refresh the spectra list.

A color value of None represents Automatic and is resolved from the active palette during rendering. Explicit per-spectrum colors continue to take precedence when the palette changes. Continuous palettes are sampled across the complete selection; the editor offers a bounded selection of representative swatches.

Both workspaces enforce LEGEND_EDITOR_MAX_ROWS = 100. Only those editor rows are instantiated, preventing large map or spectrum selections from creating thousands of Qt widgets. The dialog receives the full selection count so automatic gradient previews still match their plotted spectrum positions. Values outside the current batch remain untouched.

docs.title: View Options Synchronization & Persistence
docs.text:
The View Option menu and bottom toolbar provide user-configurable display settings arranged in a compact 2-column QWidgetAction panel (synchronized across workspaces and persisted across sessions):

  • Plot Theme (cbb_theme): Configures the Matplotlib canvas theme ("Dark Mode" or "Light Mode"), synchronized across the Spectra workspace, Maps workspace, and secondary 2D map viewer dialogs. By default, the plot theme is always set to "Light Mode" unless the user explicitly switches it to "Dark Mode". It is completely independent of the global application UI theme, and the user's explicit choice is persisted across sessions in view_options/theme.
  • Legend Placement & Outside Option (act_legend_outside): When checked, VSpectraViewer positions the legend outside the primary axes via loc="center left" and bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5). The figure's compressed layout dynamically adjusts plot margins so the legend fits cleanly without overlapping spectral traces. This setting is synchronized between Spectra and Maps workspaces and persisted across sessions in view_options/legend_outside. Legend double-click bounds detection dynamically refreshes window extents from the underlying legend artist to guarantee accurate hit-testing regardless of layout compression.
  • Colorbar Legend Mode (act_legend_colorbar, cbb_colorbar_param, le_colorbar_label): When checked (and btn_legend is enabled), VSpectraViewer replaces the discrete per-spectrum legend box with a right-side Matplotlib colorbar driven by the shared filename numeric token extractor (_extract_filename_tokens() / _extract_series_parameter_values(), shared with 2D Heatmap mode) or spectrum Index. The row_colorbar_param and row_colorbar_label rows in the 2-column options menu are shown only when act_legend_colorbar / chk_legend_colorbar is checked (_update_colorbar_options_visibility()). Parameter selections are tracked across the session by underscore token slot and normalized unit pattern (_refresh_token_combobox()), preserving the chosen parameter even when selecting different spectrum subsets whose first filename carries a different numeric value. For gradient palettes, each spectrum's automatic color is mapped directly from its extracted parameter value via _resolve_colorbar_cmap_and_norm() (custom per-spectrum color overrides continue to take priority). Persisted across sessions under view_options/legend_colorbar, view_options/colorbar_param, and view_options/colorbar_label, and synchronized between Spectra and Maps workspaces.

docs.title: Heatmap & Signal Processing Optimizations
docs.text:
• Vectorized Heatmap Matrix Interpolation: When 2D heatmap mode is active, cubic/linear Y-axis interpolation processes the entire intensity matrix simultaneously (scipy.interpolate.interp1d(..., axis=0)) rather than looping per spectral column, slashing heatmap render times by over 4× on large batches.
  • Fast Cosmic Ray / Eraser Noise Estimation: Replaced iterative sliding-window polynomial fitting with first-difference Median Absolute Deviation (\(MAD / (0.6745 \sqrt{2})\)), providing robust baseline noise estimation in \(O(N)\) vectorized NumPy time.
  • Hover Hit-Testing Pre-filter: _on_hover uses an x-range bounding pre-filter to skip expensive contains(event) line computations on irrelevant peak markers.

docs.title: VFitModelBuilder — The Controls Panel
docs.text:
File: v_fit_model_builder.py

A splitter panel containing the full preprocessing and fitting control surface:

  • Left pane: X-correction, spectral range, baseline mode selector, baseline action buttons.
  • Right pane: VPeakTable (editable parameter rows) + fit action buttons (Fit, Copy model, Paste model, Save model, Apply model).
  • Drag-and-Drop Model Loading: Accepts dropped .json fit model files directly onto the panel or via the parent workspace. When dropped, fit_model_dropped(path) triggers load_fit_model_file(), delegating to VMFitModelBuilder.load_model_file(). This loads the external model into memory, updates the model dropdown, selects it, activates the Fit Model Builder tab, and displays a floating notification. Both Spectra and Maps workspaces inherit and support this functionality.

docs.title: VPeakTable — The Parameter Table
docs.text:
File: v_peak_table.py

An interactive table where each row represents one peak. Columns show label, model shape, center (x₀), FWHM, amplitude, and bound toggles. Editing any cell emits a signal to VMWorkspaceSpectra, which updates md.fit_model and immediately reconstructs the Y_peaks preview.

docs.title: Loading Spectra
docs.text:
1. User Action: The user drag-and-drops files into the VWorkspaceSpectra UI.
  2. View → ViewModel: The View calls vm.load_files(paths).
  3. File Parsing: For each file, the ViewModel delegates to the m_io module (load_spectrum_file, load_wdf_spectrum, etc.). The IO module returns a dictionary containing raw arrays (x0, y0) and metadata.
  4. Data Storage: The ViewModel registers the data in the SpectraStore by calling add_map(name, x0, Y0, coords, fnames). A new MapData block is created with x and Y set to None (raw data only).
  5. UI Update: The ViewModel emits the spectra_list_changed signal. The View catches this and updates the VSpectraList sidebar.

The m_io module auto-detects format from file extension. Every loader returns a uniform dict:

{
    "type": "spectra",
    "items": [
        {"name": str, "x0": ndarray, "y0": ndarray, "metadata": dict},
        ...
    ]
}

WDF files may return multiple items (temporal series). All items are registered as separate MapData blocks.

docs.title: Selecting Spectra
docs.text:
1. User Action: The user clicks a spectrum in VSpectraList.
  2. View → ViewModel: The list widget emits a selection signal which calls vm.set_selected_indices().
  3. State Update: The ViewModel resolves indices to unique fnames and stores the active selection.
  4. Payload Construction: The ViewModel calls _emit_selected_spectra(), which queries SpectraStore to build a "type": "tensor_list" payload containing the arrays for all selected spectra.
  5. UI Update: The ViewModel emits spectra_selection_changed(data_dict). VSpectraViewer receives it, calls set_plot_data(), and redraws the Matplotlib canvas.

The selection payload (data_dict) contains pre-extracted arrays keyed by "type": "tensor_list" for the Spectra workspace (list of independent arrays, each potentially with a different x-axis). The Maps workspace overrides this to emit "type": "tensor" (shared x-axis matrix).

docs.title: Fitting Workflow
docs.text:
1. User Action: The user clicks "Fit" in VFitModelBuilder.
  2. Task Construction: The ViewModel builds a list of tasks (one per map/spectrum) containing indices and the fit_model dictionary.
  3. Thread Launch: The ViewModel instantiates VBFthread(store, tasks) and starts it. The UI buttons are disabled via the fit_in_progress(True) signal.
  4. Engine Execution (Background): For each task, the thread calls the VBFengine.fit_spectra(x, Y_sub, fit_model, weights).
  5. Result Storage (Background): As fits complete, the thread directly writes results to the SpectraStore via set_fit_results() and updates the Y_bestfit and Y_peaks arrays on the MapData object.
  6. Progress Updates: The thread emits progress signals which the ViewModel relays to the View's progress bar.
  7. Completion: The thread emits finished(). The ViewModel catches this, calls _on_fit_finished(), re-enables the UI, and triggers a canvas redraw.

[!NOTE] VBFthread calls store.set_fit_results() directly from the worker thread. This is safe because PySide6 allows writes to pure Python/NumPy objects from non-GUI threads, as long as no Qt widget operations occur. The finished() signal then triggers UI updates on the main thread.

docs.title: Baseline Workflow
docs.text:
1. User sets mode in VFitModelBuilder → set_baseline_settings() stores config in md.baseline_config.
  2. User clicks on spectrum → add_baseline_point(x) adds anchor to md.baseline_config["points"].
  3. preview_baseline() evaluates and stores md.Y_baseline for rendering (does not subtract).
  4. subtract_baseline() runs batch_preprocess() on the map — subtracts Y_baseline from Y, sets md.is_baseline_subtracted = True.
  5. delete_baseline() restores Y by running batch_preprocess() with an empty baseline config (crop only), resets is_baseline_subtracted.

docs.title: Peak Editing Workflow
docs.text:
1. User Ctrl+clicks peak mode on viewer → VSpectraViewer.peak_add_requested(x) → add_peak_at(x).
  2. ViewModel reads y-value at x from md.Y[spec_idx, idx], initializes peak_model dict with auto-estimated x0, ampli, fwhm, bounds.
  3. Peak dict is appended to md.fit_model["peak_models"] under the next integer key.
  4. eval_peak_initial() evaluates the model curve and appends it to md.Y_peaks.
  5. _emit_selected_spectra() triggers viewer redraw, showing the new peak curve instantly.

docs.title: Fit Results Collection
docs.text:
# VMWorkspaceSpectra.collect_fit_results()
#   → SpectraStore.build_fit_results_df()
#   → returns pd.DataFrame with columns:
#      Filename, [x0_Peak1, fwhm_Peak1, ampli_Peak1, area_Peak1, ...], R2

build_fit_results_df() is fully vectorized — it reads md.peak_params directly (no Python loop over spectra), applies user peak labels, computes area columns, appends the per-spectrum R2 column (coefficient of determination, read straight from md.fit_r2 — the same value the SpectraViewer shows for the selected spectrum), and returns a pd.DataFrame. R2 is a single scalar per spectrum (not per-peak), so collect_fit_results()'s column sort leaves it at the end of the frame. In the Spectra workspace, X and Y columns are dropped before emitting to the results table.

Decimal precision is set by build_fit_results_df(..., decimals=…), which rounds every numeric fit column (parameters, areas, R²) while leaving the X/Y coordinates at full precision — it's the single rounding authority, so collect_fit_results() no longer rounds afterwards. VMWorkspaceSpectra.results_decimals (default 3) supplies the value; the Fit Results tab's "Fit results decimals" spinbox (above the Collect button) sets it through set_results_decimals() (applied on the next Collect). compute_column_from_expression() rounds its computed column to the same results_decimals. The public API's build_fit_results_df keeps its own default of 4.

docs.title: Modern Format (v2+, ZIP-backed)
docs.text: Workspace files (.spectra) use the ZIP-backed format described in SpectraStore: Persistence. The metadata.json stores per-spectrum configuration and the arrays.npz stores the heavy numerical arrays.

docs.title: Legacy Loader
docs.text:
_load_legacy_spectra() handles .spectra files from older SPECTROview versions (raw JSON with base64+zlib-compressed arrays). It:

  1. Decodes and decompresses x0/y0 arrays.
  2. Reconstructs baseline_config, evaluates md.Y_baseline.
  3. Re-evaluates peak curves to populate md.Y_peaks and md.Y_bestfit.

No migration is required — the legacy format is loaded transparently at runtime.

docs.title: Adding a New Preprocessing Tool
docs.text:
1. ViewModel: Add a method (e.g., apply_smoothing(window, apply_all)) that calls _get_target_mds(apply_all), modifies md.Y, then calls _post_bulk_action().
  2. Model (if needed): Add a function to fit_engine/baseline.py or a new file for the algorithm.
  3. View: Add a button/control to VFitModelBuilder. Emit a new signal and connect it in VWorkspaceSpectra.setup_connections().
  4. Persistence: If the tool produces state that must survive save/load, add it to SpectraStore.to_metadata_dict() and restore it in load_map_from_npz().

docs.title: Adding a New Peak Model
docs.text:
See the dedicated VBF Engine guide. In short:

  1. Add the model function and analytical Jacobian to fit_engine/models.py.
  2. Register the model name in spectroview/__init__.py → PEAK_MODELS.
  3. Add initialization logic to VMWorkspaceSpectra._initialize_peak_params().
  4. The VPeakTable and VFitModelBuilder will auto-populate the new model in their dropdowns.

docs.title: Adding a New Viewer Rendering Feature
docs.text:
1. Add the render logic to VSpectraViewer.set_plot_data() or a dedicated private method.
  2. Add the required data to the payload dict emitted by VMWorkspaceSpectra._emit_selected_spectra().
  3. If the feature requires a UI toggle, add a QCheckBox or menu action in VSpectraViewer and connect it to a redraw call.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Spectrum doesn't appear after loading

  • Check md.is_active[0] — loading sets this to True by default, but a failed load may leave the entry in an inconsistent state.
  • Verify that _emit_list_update() is called after store.add_map().

Peak table is empty after fit

  • _emit_selected_spectra() must be called after _on_fit_finished(). Check that store.set_fit_results() populated md.param_names.

R² shows 0.0 despite successful fit

  • The fit engine sets rsquared = 0 if fit_success is False. Check md.fit_success[idx] for the spectrum in question.

_emit_selected_spectra() causes a Qt signal loop

  • Never call _emit_selected_spectra() from within a slot that is connected to spectra_selection_changed. Use a QTimer.singleShot(0, ...) to defer if necessary.

For data-model troubleshooting (preprocessing not applied, memory issues), see SpectraStore: Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Data Architecture: SpectraStore
docs.text:
SpectraStore is the single source of truth for all numerical spectral data in SPECTROview. Both the Spectra and Maps workspaces read from and write to the same store. Understanding this module is the most important step for any new contributor.

Source file: spectra_store.py

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Before SpectraStore (version before 26.24.1), SPECTROview stored each spectrum as an independent Python object. This created performance bottlenecks when working with large hyperspectral maps (thousands of spectra). The tensor-centric redesign stores all spectra for a logical "map" as contiguous NumPy arrays, enabling:

  • Vectorized preprocessing — range crop and baseline subtraction applied to the entire N×M matrix in a single operation.
  • Batch fitting — the VBF engine operates directly on the tensor without Python-level iteration.
  • O(1) map access — retrieving a map's data is a single dictionary lookup, regardless of store size.
  • Heterogeneous datasets — each map owns its own x-axis, so maps with different wavenumber ranges coexist cleanly.

docs.title: Data Hierarchy
docs.text:
SpectraStore
└── dict: _maps { map_name → MapData }
    │
    ├── MapData ("spectrum_A")          ← Spectra workspace: single spectrum (N=1)
    │   ├── x0: float64[M]             raw wavenumber axis
    │   ├── Y0: float32[1, M]          raw intensity (1 spectrum)
    │   ├── x:  float64[M_proc]        processed axis (after crop)
    │   ├── Y:  float32[1, M_proc]     processed intensity (after crop + baseline)
    │   ├── coords: float64[1, 2]      always (0.0, 0.0) for point spectra
    │   ├── fnames: ["spectrum_A"]      unique identifier
    │   ├── fit_model: dict             peak model definition
    │   ├── peak_params: float64[1, K]  fitted parameters
    │   ├── fit_success: bool[1]
    │   └── ...
    │
    └── MapData ("wafer_300mm")         ← Maps workspace: hyperspectral map (N=2500)
        ├── x0: float64[M]
        ├── Y0: float32[2500, M]        raw intensity matrix
        ├── coords: float64[2500, 2]    (X, Y) stage positions
        ├── fnames: [str × 2500]        "wafer_300mm_(x, y)" per spectrum
        ├── peak_params: float64[2500, K]
        ├── fit_success: bool[2500]
        └── ...

[!IMPORTANT] Both a single spectrum and a full hyperspectral map use the same MapData structure — they only differ in N (the number of rows). This unified model is what enables the Spectra and Maps workspaces to share the same ViewModel base class (VMWorkspaceSpectra).

docs.title: MapData — The Tensor Block
docs.text:
@dataclass
class MapData:
    """All numerical data for a single hyperspectral map."""
    name: str

MapData is a dataclass that owns all heavy arrays for one logical dataset. Its fields are organized into functional groups:

docs.title: Spectral Arrays (immutable raw + mutable processed)
docs.text:
Field Shape dtype Purpose x0 [M] float64 Original wavenumber axis — never mutated Y0 [N, M] float32 Original intensities — never mutated x [M_proc] float64 Working axis after crop/x-correction (or None → use x0) Y [N, M_proc] float32 Working intensities after all preprocessing (or None → use Y0) coords [N, 2] float64 Spatial (X, Y) positions — always (0, 0) for point spectra

[!IMPORTANT] The dual-array design (x0/Y0 vs x/Y) is the key to non-destructive preprocessing. x0 and Y0 are written once on file load and never touched again. All preprocessing produces x and Y. Calling reinit_spectra() simply sets md.x = None; md.Y = None, making the store fall back to the raw arrays.

docs.title: Per-Spectrum Metadata
docs.text: Field Length Purpose fnames N Unique string identifier for each spectrum row is_active N bool — whether this spectrum is checked in the UI list colors N Optional display color per spectrum labels N Optional user-assigned display label

docs.title: Preprocessing State (shared across all N spectra in a map)
docs.text: Field Type Purpose baseline_config dict Baseline algorithm and parameters (mode, points, coef, ...) is_baseline_subtracted bool or bool[N] Whether Y has had the baseline removed range_min / range_max float Current spectral crop boundaries xcorrection_value float X-axis shift applied (cm⁻¹) intensity_norm_factor float Multiplicative intensity normalization map_metadata dict Acquisition metadata from WDF/SPC files

docs.title: Fit Results (filled after VBF engine runs)
docs.text: Field Shape dtype Purpose peak_params [N, K] float64 Optimized parameter values fit_success [N] bool Convergence flag per spectrum fit_r2 [N] float64 Coefficient of determination per spectrum param_names list[str] — Column labels for peak_params (e.g. m01_x0, m01_fwhm) fit_model dict — Peak model definition used for fitting

docs.title: Visualization Curves (derived, for rendering only)
docs.text: Field Shape Purpose Y_bestfit [N, M_proc] Composite model curve (float32, sum of all peaks + baseline) Y_baseline [N, M_proc] Evaluated baseline curve (float32 when evaluated in batch) Y_peaks list of [N, M_proc] Per-peak LazyPeakArray views evaluated on demand per sliced row(s)

docs.title: MapInfo — Lightweight Descriptor
docs.text:
@dataclass
class MapInfo:
    name: str
    row_start: int   # always 0 (kept for API compatibility)
    row_end: int
    n_spectra: int
    n_wavenumbers: int

MapInfo is a minimal summary returned by SpectraStore.get_map_info(). It exists for API compatibility — older code that needed to know "where does this map start in the global array" still works without modification, even though the global array no longer exists. Prefer get_map_data() for direct access.

docs.title: SpectraStore — The Container
docs.text:
class SpectraStore:
    _maps: dict[str, MapData]   # per-map data blocks

SpectraStore is a thin dictionary-backed container. Its public API separates cleanly into:

docs.title: Map Registration
docs.text:
store.add_map(name, x0, Y0, coords, fnames, ...)   # register a new map
store.remove_map(name)                              # delete a map and free memory
store.reorder_maps(new_order)                       # reorder for list display

docs.title: Data Access
docs.text:
md   = store.get_map_data(name)                     # MapData — primary access
info = store.get_map_info(name)                     # MapInfo — lightweight summary
x, Y = store.get_xy_batch(name, indices)            # (processed) arrays for subset

docs.title: Fit Results
docs.text:
store.set_fit_results(name, indices, peak_params, success, r2, param_names, fit_model)
store.build_fit_results_df(name, map_type, peak_labels, only_converged, decimals)  # → pd.DataFrame
#   columns: Filename, X, Y, [Zone, Quadrant], <peak params>, R2
#   `decimals` (default 4) rounds every numeric fit column; X/Y stay full-precision.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
store.batch_preprocess(name, baseline_config, range_min, range_max)   # vectorized
store.clear_preprocess(name)                                           # reset to x0/Y0

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text:
store.to_npz_dict(name)              # heavy arrays → dict for NPZ
store.to_metadata_dict(name)         # lightweight metadata → dict for JSON
SpectraStore.load_map_from_npz(...)  # class method: restore from saved arrays

docs.title: SpectrumProxy and BaselineProxy — View Bridge
docs.text:
SpectrumProxy and BaselineProxy are read/write proxy objects that present a single-spectrum interface without duplicating any tensor data.

class SpectrumProxy:
    md: MapData       # reference to the parent tensor block
    idx: int          # row index within the tensor
    fname: str        # unique identifier

    @property
    def label(self): ...   # reads md.labels[idx]
    @label.setter          # writes md.labels[idx]

    @property
    def color(self): ...   # reads md.colors[idx]
    @color.setter          # writes md.colors[idx]

The View never holds raw arrays. When VMWorkspaceSpectra._emit_selected_spectra() prepares the payload for VSpectraViewer, it packages a list of SpectrumProxy objects alongside the array slices. This means the View can call proxy.label = "My Label" and the change automatically lands in md.labels[idx] without any explicit callback.

docs.title: Class Relationships
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class SpectraStore {
        -_maps: dict
        +add_map()
        +get_map_data() MapData
        +get_map_info() MapInfo
        +set_fit_results()
        +build_fit_results_df() DataFrame
        +batch_preprocess()
        +to_npz_dict()
        +load_map_from_npz()
    }

    class MapData {
        +name: str
        +x0: ndarray
        +Y0: ndarray
        +x: ndarray
        +Y: ndarray
        +coords: ndarray
        +is_active: ndarray
        +fnames: list
        +baseline_config: dict
        +fit_model: dict
        +peak_params: ndarray
        +Y_bestfit: ndarray
        +has_fit_results() bool
        +n_spectra: int
    }

    class MapInfo {
        +name: str
        +n_spectra: int
        +n_wavenumbers: int
        +row_start: int
        +row_end: int
    }

    class SpectrumProxy {
        +md: MapData
        +idx: int
        +fname: str
        +label: str
        +color: str
        +baseline: BaselineProxy
    }

    class BaselineProxy {
        +mode: str
        +points: list
        +is_subtracted: bool
    }

    SpectraStore "1" *-- "0..*" MapData : owns
    MapData "1" <-- "0..*" SpectrumProxy : wraps row of
    SpectrumProxy "1" *-- "1" BaselineProxy : owns
    MapInfo ..> MapData : describes

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Each spectrum or map is stored as an independent MapData block in SpectraStore._maps. There is no global array or shared index. This eliminates range arithmetic and makes deletion O(1) (del _maps[name]).

For each MapData, the store holds two array pairs:

Pair Contents Mutability x0 / Y0 Raw, file-loaded data Read-only after registration x / Y Preprocessed working data Overwritten by batch_preprocess(), deleted by clear_preprocess()

When x or Y is None, the store transparently falls back to x0 / Y0 in all access methods (get_xy_batch, set_plot_data, etc.).

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text:
ViewModels always retrieve data through SpectraStore.get_map_data(name) which returns a direct reference (not a copy) to the MapData block. This means:

  • Reads are zero-copy — no data is duplicated.
  • Writes are immediate — any modification to md.Y is visible everywhere that holds a reference to the same md.

This is why the ViewModel calls self.store.get_map_data(fname) at the start of every operation, rather than caching md as an instance variable.

docs.title: Updates and Synchronization
docs.text:
The ViewModel follows a consistent update pattern after every state change:

mutate MapData  →  _emit_selected_spectra()  →  [optional] _emit_list_update()

_emit_selected_spectra() re-reads all selected MapData blocks and emits a fresh payload to the viewer. _emit_list_update() re-reads all map names and emits status dicts for the spectra list coloring.

This pull-on-signal pattern ensures the View is always consistent with the model without needing explicit change notifications on every field mutation.

docs.title: Memory Management
docs.text:
• Y0 is stored as float32 to halve memory vs float64, with no perceptible precision loss for spectroscopy.
  • Processed arrays Y are only allocated after the first preprocessing operation.
  • Y_bestfit, Y_baseline, and Y_peaks are allocated lazily on first fit.
  • Deleting a map with store.remove_map(name) removes the dict entry; Python garbage collection releases the arrays when no other references exist.
  • Large baseline computation intermediates are not cached — they are recomputed on demand by eval_baseline_batch().

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline
docs.text:
All preprocessing is non-destructive. x0 and Y0 are always preserved.

  1. Raw Data: x0 and Y0 (immutable).
  2. Range Crop: Arrays are sliced between md.range_min and md.range_max.
  3. X-Correction: md.xcorrection_value is added to the wavenumber axis.
  4. Baseline Evaluation: SpectraStore.batch_preprocess() evaluates the baseline model for the entire tensor.
  5. Baseline Subtraction: The evaluated baseline is subtracted from the cropped intensities.
  6. Working Arrays: The final results are stored in md.x and md.Y.
  7. Downstream Usage: These working arrays are used for all visualization and fitting operations.

SpectraStore.batch_preprocess() applies range crop and baseline subtraction to the entire N×M matrix in a single vectorized call. For the Spectra workspace (N=1), this processes one spectrum. For the Maps workspace (N=2500), it processes the entire map tensor in one call.

docs.title: Modern Format (v2+, ZIP-backed)
docs.text:
Workspace files (.spectra / .maps) are ZIP archives:

Entry Content metadata.json Lightweight JSON: format_version, store_meta dict (fnames, colors, labels, baseline_config, fit_model, range bounds, xcorrection) arrays.npz NumPy compressed arrays: store_{name}_x0, store_{name}_y0, store_{name}_coords, store_{name}_peak_params, store_{name}_Y_bestfit, store_{name}_Y_peak_{i} dataframes.pkl Optional: pickled df_fit_results

The separation of lightweight JSON from heavy binary arrays enables fast metadata inspection without loading gigabytes of spectral data.

docs.title: Serialization API
docs.text:
# Save path: ViewModel → SpectraStore → WorkspaceIO
metadata = store.to_metadata_dict(name)   # JSON-serializable dict
arrays   = store.to_npz_dict(name)        # heavy NumPy arrays

# Load path: WorkspaceIO → SpectraStore
SpectraStore.load_map_from_npz(store, name, arrays, metadata)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Preprocessing not applied to viewer

  • The viewer receives md.x / md.Y from the payload. If batch_preprocess() was not called (e.g., no baseline config and no range), md.x and md.Y remain None and the viewer falls back to md.x0 / md.Y0. This is the expected non-destructive behavior.

Memory grows unboundedly with large maps

  • md.Y_bestfit, md.Y_baseline, and md.Y_peaks are never freed until the map is deleted or reinit_spectra() is called (which resets them to None). For very large maps, call store.remove_map() for maps that are no longer needed.

get_map_data() returns None

  • The map name is case-sensitive and must match the exact key used in add_map(). Check store.map_names for the registered keys.

Zero-copy semantics cause unintended side effects

  • Because get_map_data() returns a direct reference, modifying md.Y anywhere affects all consumers. Always operate through the ViewModel's established mutate-then-signal pipeline to ensure UI consistency.

docs.title: SPECTROview Theme & Design System Architecture
docs.text: This specification defines the design system, color tokens, typography, component geometry, native OS integration, and vector SVG icon engine for SPECTROview. The architecture is adapted from the production-proven design system in PLUME (commits 4af3dbb and 8242faf).

docs.title: 1. Overview & Design Philosophy
docs.text: The SPECTROview UI/UX redesign upgrades the application from legacy rasterized icons, disconnected palettes, and ad-hoc QSS overrides into a unified, token-driven scientific design system.

docs.title: PLUME Architectural Reference Commits
docs.text:
1. 4af3dbb — Core Token Engine, Integer RGBA, Native DWM & Vector Icon Engine:
  2. Central Token Bag (ThemeTokens): Frozen dataclass containing semantic color tokens rather than per-widget hardcoded colors.
  3. Synchronized QPalette (_palette_for): Maps design tokens directly to standard Qt palette roles (Window, WindowText, Base, AlternateBase, Button, Highlight, Text, etc.) ensuring native Qt widgets, item delegates, and file dialogs inherit consistent colors.
  4. Strict Integer RGBA Alpha: Qt's QSS parser rejects floating-point alpha channels (e.g. rgba(91, 140, 255, 0.25)). PLUME enforces strict integer alpha values 0..255 across all translucent tokens (e.g. rgba(91, 140, 255, 42)).
  5. Native Windows 11 DWM Title Bar Integration: Uses dwmapi.dll (DwmSetWindowAttribute) to theme native window caption, title text, and window border colors:
    • DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE (20)
    • DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR (34)
    • DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR (35)
    • DWMWA_TEXT_COLOR (36)
  6. Qt Style Hints: Automatically signals Qt.ColorScheme.Dark or Qt.ColorScheme.Light via QApplication.styleHints().setColorScheme().

  7. Vector SVG Engine (_SvgIconEngine(QIconEngine)): Replaces pre-rasterized PNGs with real-time vector rendering at 1:1 physical device pixels, eliminating downscaling blur on standard displays (96 DPI) and upscaling blur on High-DPI monitors.

  8. 8242faf — Refined Contrast, 3-Tier Hierarchy & Compact Control Geometry:

  9. 3-Tier Surface Depth:
    • Tier 0 (Rail / Root Navigation): rail_bg (#111111 Dark / #E2E5EE Light)
    • Tier 1 (Sidebars / File Trees): sidebar_bg (#161616 Dark / #EBEEF4 Light)
    • Tier 2 (Main Workspace Canvas): background (#1B1B1B Dark / #F3F4F8 Light)
    • Tier 3 (Cards / Floating Panels / Toolboxes): surface (#232323 Dark / #FFFFFF Light), surface_elevated (#2C2C2C Dark / #FFFFFF Light)
    • Sunken (Terminals / Data Tables / Logs): surface_sunken (#141414 Dark / #E8EBF2 Light)
  10. Strengthened Input & Panel Borders: Introduced dedicated input_bg, input_border, and border_strong tokens to guarantee readable contrast between active fields and surrounding containers.
  11. Compact Control Heights: Standardized single-line inputs (QLineEdit, QComboBox, QSpinBox, QDoubleSpinBox) to min-height: 18px; max-height: 22px; padding: 1px 8px; font-size: 12px (outer bounding height ~25px), preserving valuable screen real estate for spectral plots and 2D wafer maps.
  12. 18px Spinbox Controls: Replaced native OS spinners with custom 18px subcontrols utilizing dedicated SVG vector chevrons (chevron_up_{dark,light}.svg, chevron_down_{dark,light}.svg).
  13. Visible Splitters: Enhanced QSplitter::handle (5px width/height) with 1px border and centered vector grip pill SVGs (splitter_grip_{v,h}_{dark,light}.svg), resolving invisible boundary drag zones.

docs.title: 2. Theme Modes in SPECTROview
docs.text:
SPECTROview supports five persistent theme modes alongside automated migration for legacy settings:

flowchart TD
    User["User Selection / MSettings"] --> TM["ThemeManager.apply(theme_key)"]
    TM --> Decision{"Theme Key"}

    Decision -->|"dark"| ModernDark["Modern Dark (PLUME DARK_TOKENS + QSS + DWM)"]
    Decision -->|"gray"| ModernGray["Modern Gray (Office-inspired GRAY_TOKENS + QSS + DWM)"]
    Decision -->|"light"| ModernLight["Modern Light (PLUME LIGHT_TOKENS + QSS + DWM)"]
    Decision -->|"classic_dark"| ClassicDark["Classic Dark (Palette only, empty QSS)"]
    Decision -->|"classic_light"| ClassicLight["Classic Light (Palette only, empty QSS)"]
    Decision -->|"modern_warm"| Migrate["Auto-migrate to 'light' (Persist to MSettings)"]
    Migrate --> ModernLight

docs.title: 1. Modern Dark ("dark") — Flagship Deep Dark
docs.text:
• Surfaces: Neutral layered charcoal tones (#1B1B1B canvas, #161616 sidebars, #232323 cards).
  • Accents: Electric cobalt (#5B8CFF), subtle selection tint (rgba(91, 140, 255, 68)).
  • Styling: Complete global QSS, 6px control radius, 8px container radius, visible 5px splitters with grip SVGs.
  • OS Integration: Native Windows 11 immersive dark title bar (DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE = True).

docs.title: 2. Modern Gray ("gray") — Default Flagship (Soft Office Dark Gray)
docs.text:
• Default Theme: Selected by default (DEFAULT_THEME = "gray") on new installations and fresh settings profiles.
  • Surfaces: Softer neutral medium-dark gray surfaces inspired by Microsoft Word and Outlook dark-gray mode (#2B2B2B rail, #333333 chrome, #3C3C3C canvas, #454545 cards, #4E4E4E elevated controls, #5A5A5A hover).
  • Typography & Borders: Soft off-white primary text (#ECECEE) and medium-gray dividers (#5C5C5C / #6A6A6A) to prevent pure-white glare during prolonged sessions while retaining WCAG contrast.
  • Accents: Calm Office/Fluent-inspired cobalt blue (#5290F2) and translucent selection tint (rgba(82, 144, 242, 82)).
  • Normalization: normalize_theme_key() and is_dark_theme_key() in tokens.py map aliases ("modern_gray", "grey", "modern_grey") to "gray" and treat "gray" as part of the dark-family scheme for DWM title bars, SVG icon contrast, and notification badges.

docs.title: 3. Modern Light ("light") — Flagship Daylight
docs.text:
• Surfaces: Crisp cool-grey and pure white surfaces (#F3F4F8 canvas, #EBEEF4 sidebars, #FFFFFF cards).
  • Accents: Deep royal blue (#2F62F0), subtle selection tint (rgba(47, 98, 240, 48)).
  • Styling: Complete global QSS mirroring Modern Dark geometry and typography.
  • OS Integration: Native Windows 11 light title bar with light grey caption (#EBEEF4) and dark text (#141519).

docs.title: 4. Classic Dark ("classic_dark") & Classic Light ("classic_light") — Minimalist Legacy
docs.text:
• Preserves standard Qt Fusion palette styling without custom QSS stylesheets (app.setStyleSheet("")).
  • Ideal for users on remote desktop connections, low-power hardware, or those preferring unstyled native OS controls.

docs.title: 5. Retired Theme: Modern Warm ("modern_warm")
docs.text:
• The experimental "modern_warm" theme is deprecated and removed.
  • Automatic Migration: When MSettings.get_theme() or ThemeManager.apply() encounters "modern_warm", it automatically migrates the setting to "light", updates persistent storage, and applies Modern Light.

docs.title: 6. Plot Theme vs. Application UI Theme Decoupling
docs.text:
• Matplotlib Canvas Theme: In addition to the application-wide Qt UI theme, the plot canvas theme ("Dark Mode" or "Light Mode") is independently configured via the Plot theme selector in VSpectraViewer.
  • Default & Independence: The plot canvas theme defaults to "Light Mode" across all viewers and operates completely independently from the global application UI theme. Toggling the UI theme between dark, gray, and light does not alter the canvas plot theme.
  • Persistence: Explicit user selections in the plot theme selector persist across application sessions in view_options/theme.

docs.title: Typography Stack
docs.text:
• Standard UI Typography: 

    font-family: "Inter", "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
    Provides clean legibility across dense scientific property sheets and menus without requiring external bundled TTF/OTF dependencies.

  • Monospace Numerical & Code Stack: 

    font-family: "JetBrains Mono", "Cascadia Code", "Consolas", monospace;
    Used in spectral coordinate readouts, VBF parameter tables, fit residual reports, and embedded AI code snippets.

  • Font Size Safety: Application initialization guarantees positive point size (setPointSizeF(9.0)) to eliminate negative-size layout warnings during Qt Markdown rendering.

docs.title: Radii & Geometry Hierarchy
docs.text:
Corner Radii:
  ├── 8px : Large cards, group boxes, dialog containers, tab panes, menus, tooltips
  ├── 6px : Interactive controls (QPushButton, QLineEdit, QComboBox, QSpinBox)
  ├── 4px : Checkbox indicators, table row action buttons
  └── height // 2 : Capsule buttons and status badges

docs.title: Compact Control Specifications
docs.text:
In high-density scientific analysis, oversized standard controls waste critical chart space. All single-line input controls are constrained to a compact vertical budget:

QLineEdit, QComboBox, QSpinBox, QDoubleSpinBox {
    background-color: @input_bg;
    color: @text_primary;
    border: 1px solid @input_border;
    border-radius: 6px;
    padding: 1px 8px;
    min-height: 18px;
    max-height: 22px;
    font-size: 12px;
}
  • Spinbox Arrows: Width 18px, dedicated SVG vector chevrons positioned via subcontrols ::up-button, ::down-button, ::up-arrow, ::down-arrow.
  • Visible Splitter Grips: 
    QSplitter::handle:horizontal {
    width: 5px;
    background-color: @sidebar_bg;
    border-left: 1px solid @border_strong;
    image: url("splitter_grip_v_dark.svg");
}
QSplitter::handle:vertical {
    height: 5px;
    background-color: @background;
    border-top: 1px solid @border_strong;
    image: url("splitter_grip_h_dark.svg");
}
QSplitter::handle:hover, QSplitter::handle:pressed {
    background-color: @accent_tint;
    border-color: @accent;
}

docs.title: The Vector Engine (_SvgIconEngine)
docs.text:
Traditional rasterized PNG icons suffer from two major defects in desktop analytical software:

  1. Resampling blur when scaled to fractional DPRs (e.g. 125%, 150%, 175% scaling on Windows 11).
  2. Hardcoded colors that cannot adapt dynamically when toggling between Dark and Light modes.

SPECTROview resolves this via a native PySide6 QIconEngine subclass:

flowchart LR
    Caller["svg_icon('spectrum_1d', 16)"] --> Engine["_SvgIconEngine"]
    Engine --> Paint["paint(painter, rect, mode, state)"]
    Paint --> DPR["Query Device Pixel Ratio (dpr)"]
    DPR --> Phys["phys_dim = round(rect_size * dpr)"]
    Phys --> Color["Dynamic Color Resolution (text_primary vs text_muted)"]
    Color --> CacheCheck{"In _IMAGE_CACHE?"}
    CacheCheck -->|"Yes"| CachedImg["Return QImage"]
    CacheCheck -->|"No"| RenderSVG["QSvgRenderer.render(phys_dim)"]
    RenderSVG --> Boost["Edge Alpha Boost (<=22px: 1.12x)"]
    Boost --> StoreCache["Store in _IMAGE_CACHE"]
    StoreCache --> Draw["painter.drawImage(target_rect, img)"]

docs.title: Optical Stroke Compensation & Edge Alpha Boost
docs.text:
1. Geometric Path ViewBox: All icons are defined in a normalized 0 0 24 24 viewBox with stroke attributes:
  2. fill="none"
  3. stroke-linecap="round"
  4. stroke-linejoin="round"
  5. Optical Stroke Width:
  6. stroke-width="1.8" when phys_dim <= 20 (compensates for raster grid clipping at 16-20px).
  7. stroke-width="1.75" when phys_dim > 20.
  8. Sub-Opaque Alpha Boost:
  9. On standard 96 DPI displays (DPR = 1.0), 16px diagonal stroke anti-aliasing can appear faint.
  10. For phys_dim <= 22, each non-zero, non-opaque pixel (0 < alpha < 255) receives an optical 1.12x contrast boost: $\(\text{alpha}_{\text{boosted}} = \min(255, \operatorname{round}(\text{alpha} \times 1.12))\)$

docs.title: Dynamic Paint-Time Color Resolution & Multi-Tier Caching
docs.text:
• Theme-Adaptive: When svg_icon(name) is instantiated without an explicit color override, the engine resolves the active color at paint time:
  • QIcon.Mode.Normal / QIcon.Mode.Active \(\rightarrow\) tokens().text_primary
  • QIcon.Mode.Disabled \(\rightarrow\) tokens().text_muted
  • When toggling themes between Modern Dark and Modern Light, all toolbars, menus, and list items update their icon colors instantly without recreating widgets.
  • Zero-Allocation Caching:
  • _IMAGE_CACHE: (name, phys_dim, color) -> QImage
  • _PIXMAP_CACHE: (name, size, color, dpr) -> QPixmap
  • _ICON_CACHE: (name, color_override, mode_key) -> QIcon

docs.title: 6. SPECTROview Icon Inventory & Catalog
docs.text: The vector SVG catalog provides 100% vector coverage across application navigation, workspace toolbars, and scientific spectroscopy operations:

docs.title: 1. Common UI & Navigation

• sidebar: Toggle sidebar collapse / expand.

docs.title: 2. File, Dataset & Clipboard Operations
docs.text:
• folder / open: Open folder / file loader.
  • save, save_all, save_as: Save spectra, map tensors, or graph projects.
  • database: Workspace DataFrame store / spectra tensor store.
  • file_text, file_spreadsheet, file_pdf: Multi-format file indicators.
  • copy, cut, paste, duplicate: Clipboard and item duplication.
